/001-GAC_Seabadge.desc:
Seabadge is a leadership and management training focused on the “how-to” aspects of managing a successful youth-led Sea Scout program. While Seabadge was developed as an advanced leadership training program for experienced Sea Scout adult leaders, the course is open to all adult Scout leaders.  The driving theme for the training is to Focus on Youth, which makes the course especially valuable for any Scout leader working with older youth.  Seabadge does not cover topics like boating, knots, or other program-related materials found in the Sea Scout Manual.
Seabadge is a weekend course that begins Friday afternoon and concludes with a closing ceremony before lunch on Sunday.  Course participants and staff function as a model ship to help participants understand how a ship or youth-led unit should function. The curriculum includes twenty sessions, with established objectives, that are presented in a motivating and informative forum.

/001-woodbadge.desc:
Wood Badge is advanced Scout leader training that began in 1919 by Lord Baden-Powell, founder of Scouting and Wood Badge’s first director. It came to America in 1948 and has been updated to reflect current BSA policies and programs. Incorporating the best techniques available, Wood Badge has become the most advanced leadership training course in Scouting!
Wood Badge is the highest level of Scout leadership training and provides you with the tools to be a superior leader. The leadership skills taught are for leaders from all Scouting areas including Cub Scouting, Boy Scouting, Venturing and the district and council. The 1st half of the course utilizes a classroom environment and practical exercises to teach the essentials of leadership. You’ll learn what makes leadership work for you in Scouting and your personal life. The 2nd half offers classroom and outdoor experiences to help you learn the application of leadership skills. Finally, you will write and complete a “Ticket”. The “Ticket” consists of five written goals. These goals connect your new leadership knowledge to your role in Scouting.
Any Scouter who has attended basic training for their registered position and serves in a leadership role in Scouting or in a position that directly supports a unit can attend.

/003-Cub.desc:
Summer camp can be the highlight to any Cub Scout's year. It's the time to put your scout skills into action. Just the word "Scout" or "Scouting" takes people to thoughts of the outdoors. Our camp was built to create a summer camping program that is fun, adventurous, and an incredible learning experience.
The 520-acre Camp Alaflo, located outside Enterprise, Alabama, provides facilities that help create a unique and quality Scouting program. Scouts can enjoy fellowship in the air-conditioned McRight Dining Hall, Canoe in Lake Essayon, learn ecology and conservation, apply their skills at the Archery, Shotgun, and Rifle Ranges, or one of our off camp adventures.
Along with handicrafts, outdoor skills, nature and ecology, and of course our famous 1st-year camper program, Rawhide, Camp Alalfo is the summer camp that can meet the needs of your Scouts.
Mark your calendars now and make plans to join us next summer! Scouts will have a chance to choose 10 merit badges and a high adventure activity! Registration will be available soon.
We look forward to seeing you at camp.

/006-wintercamp.desc:
WINTER CAMP
JANUARY 2-4, 2027
CAMP HORNE
The staff of Winter Camp 2027 welcomes you to Camp Horne. We look forward to another successful year where your Scouts can continue to grow in their life journey through Scouting.
Winter Camp is a wonderful place to discover new friends, enjoy good food, and build lifelong skills through both Scouting and Venturing program opportunities. This year’s Winter Camp will offer some different activities and schedule from previous years! We will offer merit badge programming like that of summer camp, but Winter Camp also stresses fun through the open program activities. These activities allow Scouts to enjoy utilizing some of the skills they have learned already in Scouting.
Please review the Leaders’ Guide carefully as there are a few significant changes related to check-in, the Trailblazer program has been removed for Winter Camp, as well as introducing the Pathfinder program, designed for older Scouts to participate in specific Range and Target Activities only offered to them. There will also be several leader opportunities.  If you have any specific questions or unit requirements, please do not hesitate to let us know. We will do everything within our power to ensure your Scouts have a memorable experience and an enjoyable learning opportunity.
The Black Warrior Council is excited to offer Winter Camp 2027 and we look forward to serving your Scouts!

/011-NYLT2027.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
is an exciting, action-packed, week-long course designed to give youth members the leadership skills and experiences they can use in their home troops, crews, ships, and throughout their lives.Participants learn practical methods and skills that will help them become more confident and effective leaders. The course centers on the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must
KNOW
, and what a leader must
DO
, with a clear focus on putting those skills into action and understanding the true meaning of leadership.
Important Enrollment Requirement
The course must have a minimum of 24 participants fully registered no later than 30 days before the course start date. If there are fewer than 24 fully registered participants at the 30-day deadline, the course WILL be canceled.
Register early! Your registration helps ensure that NYLT can be held as scheduled.
Scholarships
Scholarships may be available for in-council Scouts who need financial assistance.
For scholarship information, please email
Michael.Korcheck@scouting.org.
General Participant Requirements
All NYLT participants must:
Be a currently registered member of a Scouting unit.
Have a current Annual
Health and Medical Record, Parts A, B, and C
.
Have the recommendation of their unit leader.
The recommendation may be submitted by email.
Have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, participants should be comfortable camping and preparing meals in an outdoor environment.
Scouts BSA Requirements
Scouts BSA participants must:
Be
at least 13 years old
and within the maximum age allowed for their program registration.
Be a
First Class Scout or highe
r.
Have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops (ILST).
Venturer and Sea Scout Requirements
Venturers and Sea Scouts must:
Be at least
14 years old, or 13 years old and have completed the eighth grade
, and be within the maximum age allowed for their program registration.
Have completed the appropriate unit-level leadership training:
Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews (ILSC) for Venturers
, or
Introduction to Leadership Skills for Ships (ILSS)
for Sea Scouts.
It is recommended that participants have

National Youth Leadership Training
Scouting at its best!  – 2027
Two Sessions:
Two Weekends of Feb 13-15, 19-21, 2027

Feb 15 - 4:00 PM depart

GGAC participants have registration priority
If available, Out-of-Council registration will open after December 15.
Week of June 6 - 12, 2027
Sign in at 10:00 AM Sunday, June 6
Pick-up at 1:00 PM Saturday, June 12
No unit
allowed to send more than 10 without discussion with NYLT Registrar. All must be approved by the Unit Leader.
Additional important pre- and post- course meetings will be held separately for each course; check
NYLT Website
for session details.
Cost
:  Both include camp fees, meals and course materials
Winter
: $485 until Jan 1, 2027, then $515 (February course)
June
: $515 until May 1, 2027, then $545 (June courses)
There is a $30 additional fee for Out of Council registrations.
Registration after February 1 for February Course and after May 21, 2027 for the June Courses will be waitlisted unless registration has been closed before then because the waitlist is full. Do note that the Winter course filled up for boys by late October and for girls about February 1. The last regular registration for the June course was on May 14.
Note: Except for medical or family emergencies, a minimum of $50 will be charged on cancellation requests. See other normal charges under the GGAC cancellation policies.
Questions?
Email:
ggac-nylt@comcast.net
The Scouting America NYLT course presents key leadership qualities and skills in a unique youth experience, applying modern leadership and team development theories in a contemporary scouting environment.
Participants camp, work, play and learn – living a month in the life of a model troop condensed into an intense week long or two weekend course. They experience the stages of team development, practice from a “toolbox” of leadership skills and learn that leadership requires vision, goals, and planning.
Participants learn how to be a leading influence in their own unit; discovering resources, methods, games and new skills to make unit meetings, treks and other activities more exciting and worthwhile. They also develop skills that help them emerge as leaders outside their units – at school and in the community.
Who may attend?
Qualified candidates will meet the following criteria…
First Class Scouts who are at least 13 years of age at the start of the course or Venture Crew members.
Scouts are required to be 1st Class or above at least 30 days before course.
Currently serve in a youth leadership position, or possess the skills and ambition to undertake a role in leadership.
Have completed Troop/Crew Leadership Training in their unit.
Are comfortable with long-term camping.
Are approved and endorsed by their unit leaders
as exhibiting maturity, with a positive attitude, focus and aspirations to serve through leadership.
Commitment to attend the full course, all sessions.
Note: To enable broad council participation and the best youth experience, the number of participants from each unit may be limited. Additional reservations and out-of-council registrations are subject to availability.
Note also:  For each session, we do maintain two separate registration links, based on gender. This helps us in balancing male and female registration numbers. NYLT, Nationally, does run under the Family Troop model which means that there may be all male patrols, all female patrols, or patrols with a mix of both males and females.
For the Winter session, we will have mixed gender patrols; this will be discussed in more detail at the first Troop Meeting / Orientation on January 27, 2027.
For the June session, the likely breakdown will be two all-male Troops, one all-female Troop, and one “Family” Troop primarily with single-gender patrols. However, there may be a few mixed-gender patrols. This will be discussed at the May 6th Orientation

/032-Tahquitz2027.desc:
Camp Tahquitz: Making Memories Since 1925
For more than a century, the Long Beach Area Council, Scouting America, has delivered one of the premier camping and outdoor programs in the country. Camp Tahquitz, our crown jewel in the San Bernardino Mountains, has one simple goal: Making Memories for every Scout who walks through our gates.
A Square Mile of Mountain Wilderness
The Long Beach Area Council is fortunate to own a full square mile of land at 6,500 feet elevation, where giant ponderosa pines tower over rolling green meadows and the air is clean and cool all summer long. With traditions dating back to 1925, Camp Tahquitz has served thousands of youth from the greater Long Beach area and surrounding councils. Thanks to careful stewardship, large sections of the property remain in their natural state, preserved for the Scouts of today and generations to come.
Perched on the edge of the San Gorgonio Wilderness Area, camp offers spectacular views of the peaks above and the valley below, abundant birds and wildlife, and gateway access to challenging backcountry hikes through some of Southern California's most magnificent terrain.
Facilities & Program
Beyond the classic camp essentials of dining hall, shooting ranges, pool, and lake, Tahquitz features secluded outpost camps, a wide-ranging orienteering course, a COPE course, a climbing wall, and four historic log cabins lovingly preserved and adapted as program centers.
Our program offers something for every Scout: archery, rifle, and shotgun shooting; horsemanship; handicraft; outdoor skills; hiking; nature studies; and much more. Whatever your Scouts are excited about, they'll find it here.
A Staff That Makes the Difference
Ask anyone who's been to Tahquitz and they'll tell you: our greatest asset is our staff. Every member of our youth staff belongs to the Tahquitz Community and
volunteers
to serve at summer camp out of genuine dedication to Scouting and a desire to help other Scouts learn and grow. Chosen for their outstanding character and abilities, they have been planning and training since September, and most Area Directors are graduates of National Camping School. Their only goal is to serve your troop and make this the best summer camp experience your Scouts have ever had.
Getting Here
Camp Tahquitz sits on California Highway 38, just 26 miles beyond Redlands, about a two-hour drive from Long Beach. A paved road leads from the highway right into central camp.
Join us this summer and see why Scouts have been making memories at Camp Tahquitz for over 100 years.

/033-20MileHike.desc:
Date & Time:
Saturday, December 5, 2025 (7:00am - 7:00pm)
Cost:
Free Registration
Join us on our 20-mile hike to help you complete the Hiking Merit Badge. This is a strenuous 20 mile hike of the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail in the Angeles National Forest.
This is an out-and-back hike where we hike 10 miles into the wilderness along the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail. There are 56 stream crossings to wade. We have found that what works best is to wear trail runners or sturdy athletic shoes and simply wade across the streams and hike with wet feet. Leave a pair of dry pair of shoes in the car for the ride home. Recommended socks are merino wool socks (best), or synthetic athletic socks (no cotton). We will finish the hike in full darkness, about 1.5 hours after sunset.
We will hike at a relaxed pace with plenty of rest stops. Scouts will call or text parents mid-afternoon with the exact time to be picked up. Parents are also welcome to join us on the hike. Registration closes on Friday, November 27th.
We will meet at 7:00 am.
We will have a brief coordination meeting on Zoom two days before the hike (Thursday at 7:30 PM)
Parents and scoutmasters are welcome to hike with us, but adults must be in shape, i.e. have completed several lengthy hikes fairly recently. Parents can sign up as part of their Scout's registration.
What to Bring:
Be prepared for rain and nightfall: bring a flashlight and raingear (at least a disposable poncho)
Bring plenty of trail snacks that are high-carb
Bring lunch and water (2 liters of water)
Bring small first aid kit
Wear hiking attire: quick-dry clothes are preferable, no blue jeans.
Sun protection: hat, sunglasses and sunscreen
Warmth item: may get breezy or chilly
Map and compass: Map will be provided, bring a compass if you have one.
Cell coverage: expect to lose cell phone coverage during most of the hike
Hiking Merit Badge book or worksheet
Signed blue card
Comfortable shoes like running shoes or hiking boots
Lightweight Jacket
Day pack
if rain is forecast, bring a poncho or raincoat

/033-WildernessWomanTrainingForMen.desc:
This course is designed specifically for male Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters serving in troops that welcome female Scouts. Creating a positive, respectful, and supportive environment begins with confident, well-prepared leadership. When adult leaders feel comfortable and confident working with all Scouts, they help foster that same confidence and sense of belonging among the youth they serve.
Throughout this course, we will explore practical approaches to addressing situations that may arise both on and off the trail, effectively leading troops with boys and girls, and maintaining appropriate boundaries in accordance with Scouting America's Youth Protection Training guidelines.
We will also discuss how to model the values of the Scout Oath and Scout Law while promoting respect, inclusion, and open communication throughout the troop.
While some of these conversations may address sensitive or unfamiliar topics, they are essential to building strong leadership skills and ensuring a safe, welcoming, and rewarding Scouting experience for every youth.

/033-WinterCampingandTravelTraining.desc:
PURPOSE:
Acquaint the adult Scouter with an understanding of the winter environment and to emphasize those backpacking skills which are necessary to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience.
DATE:
Seminar: Saturday, November 7, 2026
Weekend trip: Saturday, Sunday 6, 7 February 2027
TIME:
8:00 a.m. to about 6:00 p.m.
LOCATION:
Cushman Walt Scout Center
EQUIPMENT:
Paper and pencil, and lunch for seminar. Each Scouter is responsible for obtaining the clothing, equipment, and food for the weekend trip including snow shoes for the weekend outing.
MAXIMUM SIZE:
12 Students.
OVERVIEW:
The seminar is conducted as a series of presentations and demonstrations. The emphasis is on preparing for, and dealing with, a mountainous winter environment, be it rain, cold, snow, or some combination. Sessions cover: the physical demands of winter conditions; snow travel hazards & equipment needs; health & safety; navigation and route finding; menus; food & water needs; and personal clothing & equipment. The desirability of having a “Plan B” and the necessity of providing for unexpected changes in the weather or trail conditions are explained. Participants are invited to attend the Snow and Ice Travel seminar that follows it (see the separate training bulletin). The weekend field trip provides the opportunity to demonstrate the specific skills taught in the seminar in a winter environment. It will be a backpack in Mt. San Jacinto State Park of about 5 miles, round trip, from 8,600 to 10,000 feet. Snowshoes will be worn while backpacking.
REQUIREMENTS:
Completion of Adult Leader Backpack Training. Annual Health and Medical Record (parts A and B).
QUESTIONS:
Dennis Cline, Course Director, at (310) 792-0544; e-mail:

.

2026 National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is a dynamic, 6-day program designed to empower youth members with essential leadership skills and experiences that can be applied in their Scouts BSA Troops, Venturing Crews, Sea Scout Ships, schools, and beyond. NYLT blends the best of modern leadership techniques with the core values and traditions of Scouting. The course focuses on developing a leader’s mindset, knowledge, and actions, with a strong emphasis on how to apply these skills in real-world scenarios.
NYLT offers both classroom-based instruction and hands-on outdoor activities, culminating in a Leadership Challenge that allows participants to showcase their newfound abilities in a practical setting. This program is an exciting opportunity for youth to grow as leaders and prepare for future success in all areas of life.
Course Dates: Nov. 6th - 8th AND Nov. 13th - 15th
Important note: To graduate from NYLT, participants must be present for the entire course, including the Mandatory Pre-Course Orientation.

Must have earned First Class Rank by Nov 6th, 2026.
Completion of ILST (Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops).
Must have Unit Leader’s approval to attend NYLT.
For Ventures and Sea Scouts:
For Venturers and Sea Scouts: Must be at least 14 years old (or 13 and have completed eighth grade) and no older than 20.
Must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships and have basic camping experience.
Must have Unit Leader’s approval to attend NYLT.
Join us for this extraordinary leadership development experience that will prepare you for leadership roles now and in the future!
Note: If the scout needs to apply for a scholarship to attend the course, please contact Marie Becvar at Marie.Becvar@scouting.org.

2026 Univerity of Scouting
November 14, 2026
This years theme is
"Drive Success!"
The University of Scouting is the Greater California Council's p
remier adult training event,
designed to help Cub, Scout BSA, Venturer, Sea Scout Leaders, Parents, and Volunteers
build the knowledge and skills needed to deliver an outstanding program for their youth.
Participants do not need to be registered in Scouting America to attend this training.
This in-person-only event features a wide variety of courses tailored to every level of experience, offering practical training, fresh ideas, and valuable resources you can take back to your unit. Beyond the classroom, participants enjoy a day of fellowship, networking, sharing best practices, and connecting with fellow volunteers who are passionate about Scouting.
Whether you're new to Scouting or a seasoned leader, the University of Scouting provides an exciting opportunity to learn, grow, and strengthen your ability to deliver the best possible experience for the youth you serve.
Location -
Frances Ellen Watkins Harper Jr. High School   4000 E. Covell Blvd., Davis CA. 95618
Please read everything in the UOS catalog as there is additional information inside!
The Frequently Asked Questions page in the attachments will help with your registration process.
Den Chief Training
Scout BSA, Venturer, and Sea Scouts interested in serving as a Den Chief should ideally be at a First-Class Scout rank level or higher to attend this 3 ½ hour training course (Sessions  1-4). As a Den Chief, you serve as role models for the Cub Scouts you mentor and represent the highest standards of leadership within the pack.
Den Chief Registration is $30.00
(with lunch option available $15.00 at registration) and will include a copy of the Den Chief training book, training cords, certificate, name tag, UOS patch, folder, paper, pen and UOS facility.
The scout can sign up for any class in the 5th session to finish out the day.
Den Chief's will need a medical form AB.
The class limit is 24
Adult Investment
Adult Registration is $25.00
and you will receive a great program selection, University of Scouting Patch, a folder with paper, pen, handouts, the UOS facility, and a google drive location that will contain all the handouts or other items the instructors want to share. Also included are instructor activities, a campus map, and your schedule with classroom numbers. Be sure to check out the “Pit Stop Midway” where all our community partners will be showcasing the many activities you can participate in with your unit.
Check-in for everyone from 7:30AM-8:25AM
will be in the multipurpose room. (Look for signs)
Line up by last name to pick up your folder  that will include your schedule and map of the campus, paper, pen, patch and lunch ticket if you purchased a lunch at registration. Then proceed to the gym for our opening.
Instructors
can check-in starting at 7:15AM  in the mutipurpose room to pick up your folder and class schedule with map.
When registering, you will have the option to purchase a Togo’s Sandwich Box Lunch f
or an additional $15.00. Each box lunch includes:
Your choice of one sandwich with vegetables and wheat/white bread:
Roast Beef (no cheese)
Ham & Swiss Cheese
Turkey & Avocado (no cheese)
Turkey & Cheddar Cheese
Chicken & Cheddar Cheese
Cali Veggie & Provolone Cheese & Avocado
Bag of Lays potato chips
Chocolate Chip Cookie
Bottle of water
All condiments, pepperoncini’s, bottle of water, and napkins will be on the side.
The  Order of the Arrow (OA) snack table will also have sodas, coffee, and hot chocolate available to purchase.
OR
bring your own lunch
. There is nothing close to the school to purchase food and get back in time to enjoy the “Pit Stop Midway” the multiple community partners, the Scout Store and activities in the quad.
From 11:50AM-1:10PM
please visit the “Pit Stop Midway” in the multipurpose room to visit with the variety of youth driven organizations that will support your scouting adventure

Fall asleep to the sounds of the forest and wake up in the crisp, cool mountain air. Experience magical sunsets over the waters of the lake. /053-Nov2026IOLSBALOO.desc:
NOTE: This registration is for BALOO or IOLS Training. THIS IS COUNCIL-WIDE TRAINING - ALL SCOUTERS ARE WELCOME
Date: November 7-8, 2026  (This is an OVERNIGHT, IN PERSON training session)
Location:  Camp Rancho Alegre - 2680 CA-154, Santa Barbara, CA 93105 * (May be subject to change)
Arrival: Saturday, November 7 at 10:00 AM for time to set up camp
Departure: Sunday, November 8 at 11:00 AM
Meals: Saturday - Lunch, Dinner & Cracker Barrel. Sunday - Breakfast & To-go snack
Cost: $35
Accommodations: All participants will be in tents. One man, three-man, or family size with an air mattress are acceptable. But no hammocks or campers. If you or your unit doesn’t have access to a tent, let the course director know and arrangements may be made.
The course director will contact participants with additional information on what to bring.
BALOO stands for Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation. It’s the introductory training Cub Scout leaders should complete before taking Cub Scouts on an overnight camping trip.
Scouting America requires that Packs have at least one BALOO-trained adult on every Cub Scout den or pack overnight outdoor event. That include pack camping and Webelos patrol overnighters.  A BALOO-trained leader should be at any overnighter regardless of whether it is a pack, district or council event.
Having at least two BALOO-trained adults will make your Cub Scout Pack camping experience as awesome as it can be.
BALOO also includes a 35-minute online pre-requisite that is available from my.scouting.org in the BSA Learning Center.
Prerequisite for the course:
SYT- Safeguarding Youth Training (formerly youth protection training)
Online training component- accessed through your My.Scouting.org account.
Annual health medical record parts A and B – will be returned at end of the course
IOLS stands for Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills. IOLS training helps leaders gain confidence in their ability—through hands-on, practical application of skills and proven methods—to influence growth in positive ways to achieve the purposes of Scouting America.
The IOLS course builds and expands on the concepts and themes introduced in Scoutmaster Position-Specific Training and provides Scouters with the confidence to take youth into the outdoors.
IOLS is required for all Scoutmasters/Assistant Scoutmasters to be considered Trained for their leadership position.  Every Scout needs and deserves trained leaders.
Prerequisite for the course:
SYT- Safeguarding Youth Training (formerly youth protection training)
Annual health medical record parts A and B – will be returned at end of the course

/055-118157.desc:
Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (iOLS) is a hands-on training open to all registered adults. It teaches adult leaders how to successfully run a Scouts BSA camp-out and teaches the practical skills needed in Scouts BSA. This is a required training for all Scoutmasters and ASMs but everyone is welcomed.
On
Friday March 12, 2027
, we'll assemble at Chesebrough at 6 p.m. for check-in, campsite selection and setup, and to begin instruction.
Please bring a completed Annual Health and Medical Record - Parts A, and B, # 680-001, 2019 Printing.
http://www.scouting.org/filestore/HealthSafety/pdf/680-001_AB.pdf
Please wear your Scout uniform, and bring rain gear and layers, as the weather may change rapidly in the Santa Cruz mountains (and it’s never the same as in the valley). Please bring a mug and/or water bottle, Scout BSA Handbook and pen & paper. Please eat dinner before you arrive, or bring a “no-prep” meal with you. We will provide the ingredients, and you will prepare all your meals for Saturday and Sunday.
The Patrols (this means you) will be putting on a Campfire on Saturday. Bring some ideas/skits/songs/stories/run-ons, etc. to aid the process. Please let us know if you have any physical limitations, special dietary or medical needs so we can Be Prepared before the course begins.
You will be outdoors most of the time. Your campsites will be about 200 yards (uphill) from the parking area. You will be required to carry your gear, you will not be able to drive to the campsite.
Overnight gear, outdoor essentials and appropriate clothing are the heart of camping equipment. Please refer to the Scout BSA Handbook, chapter 9, “Camping.”
You should bring:
Appropriate closed toed foot wear - you’ll be outside on rocky, wooded, uneven, unpaved terrain
Hat
Scouts BSA Handbook
Scout Uniform (wear)
Notebook, pen
Water bottle/canteen, cup
Personal First Aid Kit, suitable for hiking
Tent (consider sharing if you know other participants)
Sleeping Bag, pad
Rain gear
Jacket, gloves (including work gloves),
Layers of clothing (to adjust to varying temperatures and varying levels of exertion) - It can get hot and cold at Chesebrough!
Pocket Knife
Flashlight
Compass
Toiletries
Scout Outdoor Essentials
Personal eating ware - utensils, plate/bowl, cup (we provide the “cooking” ware)
If you don’t have the appropriate equipment you may be able to borrow items from others in your unit.

/055-BearPaw27.desc:
Come to our 36th Annual BearPaw
OUTDOOR SESSION
Three-day Winter Camping Experience
WHAT:
The outdoor camping experience allows participants to put into practice what they learned during troop meetings, which is camping in the snow or a very cold environment within a very safe environment accompanied by a couple of hundred fellow Scouters.  This may be the best high adventure they may ever participate in as a youth; even adults have fun.  The event has a focus on fun in the cold/snow, along with camping challenges that are easily overcome with experience and mentoring.
WHEN:
February 19th - 21st or March 5th - 7th
WHERE:
Camp Hi-Sierra – 29211 Hwy 108 Long Barn, CA 95335
COST:
Bearpaw #1 $35 per participant early registration, before and on 10/31, $40 starting 11/1, $45 starting 1/31.
Bearpaw #2  $35 per participant early registration, before and on 11/30, $40 starting 12/1, $45 starting 1/31.
Price includes campground fees, cracker barrell, dining hall access, unit ribbon, and patch with rocker for each participant.
Schedule
Friday: Noon – 10 PM check-in, set up camp/build snow shelters. A leaders’ orientation will be held that evening at camp Headquarters. There will be snacks and board games in the dining hall!
Saturday activities are up to the individual units; however, games will be available for fun on Saturday morning on the athletic field such as volleyball, ultimate Frisbee, soccer on freshly packed snow, or any other event the youth wish to organize. Ice cave and snowman competitions! Sledding on the hill!! Hot cocoa!!!
Sunday morning: Clean up, pack the cars, and be checked out by 11:00 AM.
BearPaw can be considered a car camping event.  Units may leave the campground during the day on Saturday and drive up to Lake Pinecrest, go skiing, or participate in any other activity desired.  BearPaw focuses on camping in cold weather with or without snow which includes cooking, sleeping, and keeping warm.  Units are not required to be at camp during the day.
Registration Note:
Please register before the event so we have an accurate count of attendees.
Cabins:
There will be cabins available for rent, there is limited availability. Please email camping@svmbc.org. You will still need to register for the event if you or your unit is renting a cabin.
For additional details, contact Monte Crawford, Event Director, montecrawford@gmail.com or call 408.582.3993 or Dylan Hendrickson at Camping@SVMBC.org or 408.638.8312.

/055-CHS27.desc:
Welcome to Camp Hi-Sierra - Adventure lives here.
Camp Hi-Sierra sits at 5,000 feet in the heart of the Stanislaus National Forest, surrounded by towering pines and crystal-clear skies. The North Fork of the Tuolumne River winds through camp, offering a constant soundtrack of nature and possibility.
This is where Scouts come to test themselves—climbing granite walls, paddling across alpine lakes, forging iron in the blacksmith shop, and hiking rugged trails. Whether you're crafting a custom leather project, diving into wilderness survival, or exploring the stars through our new observatory, there's something here for every kind of Scout.
With over 60 merit badges, daily hikes and bike rides, epic evening programs, open shoot and swim times, and new adventures like cowboy action shooting, the Clavey River overnighter, and hands-on vocational experiences in welding and public health, Camp Hi-Sierra brings the Scouting program to life like nowhere else.
This is a place to explore, to lead, to learn, and to grow.
Launch Your 2027 Stellar Adventure!

/055-MountainRendezvous2027.desc:
Call to Rendezvous at Fort Chesebrough!
This is a 1840s event emphasizing the lifestyle of the old trapper days for Scouts BSA Troops and Crews. The time is set from 1825 - 1840 when the first Rendezvous was held. So, if you can, please dress, camp and eat as in the 1800. Think of this as a Camporee in the frontier! Don't miss out on this one-of-a-kind event for our Council. Your scouts will be transported to a different time for an amazing experience and learn period-oriented skills.
Come for the Indian fry bread and fresh churned ice cream, stay for the campfires and fellowship!

Where else can you shoot black powder rifles, throw tomahawks and knives, make fresh Indian fry bread, churn ice cream, and learn to live in the mountains?

Tents, chairs, candle lanterns, tables, 1840’s era dress, trade goods (clamshells, abalone shells, deer antlers), and camp equipment for judging
Cost:
Are $50.00 by 9/15, $55.00 by 10/1, $60.00 onsite (Food not included)
SM(s) Will have:
Youth under18; Signed Parental Release Shooting Forms and a Complete List of All attendees.

(Advanced Aged Rendezvous Person) will compete against each other. The Rendezvous Run is a special by invitation only event for the top competitors chosen by the staff.
For you Greenhorns you don't need to spend a lot of money on a Rendezvous outfit, go to goodwill or a thrift shop look an old felt hat, a plaid colored shirt old style, cut off the buttons and collar, Sew the shirt together where the buttons were, look for white painters pants, if not there go to a paint store, then cut  out all the belt looks. /055-NYLT27.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is an intensive, interactive experience in outdoor living and leadership skills development. Youth staff members work throughout the year to plan and develop the week-long training and conduct the course. Experienced and trained adult leaders closely and continually monitor all elements of the program.
NYLT is an opportunity for Scouts/Venturers/Sea Scouts to develop leadership skills that will help them better serve their own units. The training week is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home units and in other situations that demand leadership of self and others. We invite you to be a part of this growth experience!
Early Bird discount until May 1st so sign up early!
Who can attend:
In order to attend a NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C in CampDoc.
Scouts BSA members must be at least 13. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops. Scouts are also required to earn the First Class rank before attending NYLT.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships.
It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation

Go on a magical adventure, defeat monsters, and solve puzzles at the Grand Moot!
Every five years, representatives of the villages of the Ostuc region come together for a Grand Moot to reaffirm friendships, trade stories, and decide how to pool their resources for the coming years. The villages that attended the last Grand Moot had a particularly eventful gathering, and while they work on fulfilling their projects, other villages in the region will now arrive to solve their own set of goals and threats.
Grand Moot is an outdoor adventure roleplaying scenario (OARS) where each Scout will take on the role of a villager attending Grand Moot. Each villager has different magical abilities and attributes - similar to classes in a videogame or tabletop game - and must work together to complete various scenarios. Scouts can roleplay with NPCs, defeat monsters in fast-paced physical combat, explore the beautiful trails of Hi Sierra, and negotiate with other Scouts to advance their village's goals.

Come see what adventures await at this year's Grand Moot!

/055-SeaB27.desc:
Seabadge is a leadership and management training focused on the “how-to” aspects of managing a successful youth led Sea Scout program. While Seabadge was developed as an advanced leadership training program for experienced Sea Scout adult leaders the course is open to all adult Scout leaders.  The driving theme for the training is to “Focus on Youth”, which makes the course especially valuable for any Scout leader dealing with older youth.  Seabadge does not cover topics like boating, knots, or other program-related materials found in the Sea Scout Manual.
Overview & Purpose
Seabadge is a two-weekend course that begins Friday afternoon and concludes on the following Sunday with a closing ceremony.  Course participants and staff function as a model ship to help participants understand how a ship or youth-led unit should function. The curriculum includes twenty sessions, with established objectives, that are presented in a motivating and informative forum.
The objectives of Seabadge are to:
Improve the understanding of leadership, management, and motivational skills among adult leaders.
Provide management, leadership, and presentation skills and tools to adult leaders so that they may use and share them with others in their day-to-day Scout activities.
Use the skills and tools acquired at Seabadge to improve the quality of the Sea Scout program.
Encourage the development of lifelong contacts and sharing of resources by and between course participants and staff
Participant Requirements
Course applicants must meet the following minimum standard requirements prior to consideration for participation in a Seabadge course:
Is a registered adult member of Scouting America.
Has completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position and Leader Specific: Sea Scout Adult Leader Basic training.
Have a tablet or computer with a screen large enough to view the materials being presented, a webcam and a stable internet connection
Participate in a minimum of 2 pre-course Crew meetings (via Zoom) to plan and prepare your Crew Project
Uniform Requirements
Sea Scout participants should wear the Official Sea Scout Uniform as described in the Sea Scout Manual. Other Scout participants should wear their official Scouting uniform (official Scout leader shirt, Scout pants, leather or web belt, and official socks).
Logbook
Prior to the course, you will work with your Crew Advisor to develop your Logbook. The Logbook is a series of goals you will complete over 6-18 months after the course.
Your completion certificate and trident will be mailed to the address you register with after completing your logbook.

/055-Venturing27CHS.desc:
Older Youth Adventure Week | Camp Hi-Sierra
Older Youth Adventure Week
Shoot. Climb. Explore. Plan Your Own Adventure.
This is not your typical week at camp.
Older Youth Adventure Week at Camp Hi-Sierra, in the Sierra Nevada mountains just north of Yosemite, is built for Scouts ages 13* through 20 who want more challenge, more independence, and experiences you will not find during a regular summer camp session. From advanced shooting sports to real rock climbing to a youth-planned adventure day at Pinecrest, this week is active, hands-on, and built around you.
What You Will Do
Spend the week rotating through advanced shooting sports, including rifle, shotgun, archery, cowboy action, and specialty activities based on range availability. Learn real climbing skills and practice lead climbing techniques at camp.
Midweek, you and your crew will plan and execute your own Pinecrest adventure within staff guidelines. You will build the plan, pitch it, and carry it out.
And yes, you still get campfires, observatory nights, black powder shooting, board games, and time with friends.
What Parents and Leaders Should Know
This program is open to all registered Scouts ages 13* through 20. *13-year-olds must have finished the 8th grade. Scouts can work on the trail to Ranger and Summit if they want to.
Scouts are organized into small crews of fewer than 10, so you are with people who want to do similar activities together.
Adults are welcome as additional supervisors, but this is a youth-led experience. Scouts are expected to take ownership of their learning, decision-making, and adventure planning throughout the week.

/055-wbspring2027.desc:
For Chinese language:
Spring 2027 Flyer in Chinese
In 1911, Baden-Powell took the first steps in training Scouting’s adult leaders by organizing a series of lectures for  Scouters.  He made great strides in the years that followed, culminating in 1919 with the establishment of Wood Badge training. Wood Badge recipients now number more than a hundred thousand, and can be found in all corners of the world.
The objective of a Wood Badge course is to demonstrate the aims and methods of Scouting, and use them to develop stronger adult leaders. Five days (two weekends) in duration, the course is a multi-faceted presentation of leadership skills, organizational tools, and hand-on activities based on the best of Scouting traditions and the latest in team-development theory. In addition, participants will enjoy the fellowship of learning alongside many other volunteers and will have a great deal of fun.
This will be a tremendous opportunity for you to:
Understand Scouting as a family of interrelated, values-based programs providing age-appropriate activities for youth.
Recognize contemporary leadership concepts utilized in corporate  America and in leading government organizations, and discover how these concepts are relevant to our values-based movement.
Apply the skills you learn from your participation as a member of a successful working team to provide your Scouting unit with renewed leadership to accomplish its mission.
Revitalize your commitment to Scouting by sharing in an inspirational experience.  Many Scouters consider Wood Badge to be one of the peak experiences of their Scouting careers. It has served as a source of training and inspiration to thousands. In return, Wood Badge participants have affected the lives of millions of youth.
We sincerely hope that you can participate. You will enjoy it fully and benefit from it immensely. You are to be commended for the work you are doing now in scouting. Wood Badge training will enable you to make an even greater contribution as you help deliver the promise of Scouting.

Polar CUBS @ JNW
Calling all Polar Cubs for this exciting winter day camp adventure run by the JNW Outdoor Program Team. This winter, we will offer awesome activities for Cubs and friends!   Cubs will work on craft adventures, BB, Archery, winter activities, and possibly sledding. Each Saturday will run from
9 a.m. to 3 p.m.,
and
lunch will be provided
.
Check-in will open at 8:15 am, and the program will start at 9 AM. Indoor activities will be available to warm up, but please dress for the weather.
Please bring a
Health Form
A&B for
ALL
Cubs and Adults for check-in.
Polar Cubs is open to all Cub Scouts and their families;
Lions and Tigers must have an adult with them as a 1:1
We suggest a minimum of 1 adult for every two children.
WHAT SHOULD I BRING TO CAMP?
Polar Cubs is a single-day program - however, due to the unpredictable nature of our winter weather, we encourage everyone to
dress in layers
and maybe
bring extra layers
just in case! Jack Frost won't keep us down - to make sure you don't miss out on any of the arctic activities, we recommend you have the following layers:
The base layer
- AVOID COTTON fabrics touching your skin! Cotton will absorb water, which can quickly turn into cold toes and fingers! We recommend synthetic fibers such as polyester and nylon.
Warmth Layer
- This will be where the bulk of your warmth comes from. We recommend fabrics such as wool, polar fleece, or flannel. This is the perfect opportunity to dig out the ugly Christmas sweaters and fuzzy pajama pants!
Wind/Water Layer
- Your outermost layer should be wind and waterproof. Most jackets and snow pants have this built-in - but if not, you can throw a rain jacket over the top of a fleece jacket for the same effect!
Please also make sure that everyone has a water bottle. You will be doing a lot of moving around, and it is just as easy to get dehydrated in the winter as in the warm summer months!  We also suggest a small backpack to carry water and extra items.
A reminder that per the BSA's National Shooting Sports policy, Lion Scouts cannot shoot BB Guns but are more than welcome to participate in Archery.

Per Youth partisipant &
$10
Per Adult

/066-117996.desc:
Wood Badge is advanced Scout leader training that began in 1919 by Lord Baden-Powell, founder of Scouting and Wood Badge’s first director. It came to America in 1948 and has been updated to reflect current BSA policies and programs. Incorporating the best techniques available, Wood Badge has become the most advanced leadership training course in Scouting!
Wood Badge is the highest level of Scout leadership training and provides you with the tools to be a superior leader. The leadership skills taught are for leaders from all Scouting areas including Cub Scouting, Boy Scouting, Venturing and the district and council. The 1st half of the course utilizes a classroom environment and practical exercises to teach the essentials of leadership. You’ll learn what makes leadership work for you in Scouting and your personal life. The 2nd half offers classroom and outdoor experiences to help you learn the application of leadership skills. Finally, you will write and complete a “Ticket”. The “Ticket” consists of five written goals. These goals connect your new leadership knowledge to your role in Scouting.
Any Scouter who has attended basic training for their registered position and serves in a leadership role in Scouting or in a position that directly supports a unit can attend.

/070-nramuzzleloading.desc:
NRA/BSA Training Course –
Basic + Instructor for Muzzleloader Rifle
Cherokee Scout Reservation (CSR)
3296 Boy Scout Camp Road, Yanceyville, NC 27379
NOTE: CANDIDATES MUST HAVE CURRENT BIT and be current NRA Rifle Instructor to attend.
Part I: BASIC is Saturday 12/12
Saturday 8:00 am to 6 pm
Part II: INSTRUCTOR is Saturday 12/12 - Sunday 12/13
Saturday 7 - 9pm, then Sunday 8am - 4pm.
About the Weekend - Basic is on Saturday followed by Instructor.  Leave with your ML Rifle Instructor certification in one weekend.  You MUST HAVE CURRENT BIT and you MUST be an NRA Rifle Instructor.
FOR COURSE CANDIDATES
WHO MAY ATTEND:  A registered Adult BSA Leader who meets the prerequisites.  If you have any questions or concerns, reach out to course director beforehand. The Instructor certification allows you to facilitate unit Shooting Sports programs on an approved range for Muzzleloading rifle fun shoots at BSA camps.
NRA PRE-QUALIFICATIONS:
A) NRA Basic Instructor Trainer (BIT) - Mandatory within 24 months.
B) Current NRA Rifle Instructor - we will be spending time on Muzzleloading, NOT on fundamentals of rifle shooting.  Rifle fundamentals and teaching methodology is required to fit everything into one weekend.
The Part II session
WILL NOT
include Basic Instructor Training (BIT). To opt-out, proof of your previous BIT is required before enrollment is confirmed.  Acceptable date for bit is after December 12, 2024 or newer. (24 mo)  Contact the Education Team for schedule modification instructions.
COURSE OFFERING:   ONE Day basic and ONE Day instructor
1.
Basics of Muzzleloader Rifle Shooting
Indoor Instruction, Safety Exercises and Range Qualification
Short Description: This 9 hour course teaches the basic knowledge, skills and attitude necessary for the safe use of a muzzleloader rifle in BSA programs. The sessions include classroom instruction and time on a range shooting a muzzleloading rifle. Students learn the NRA’s three rules for safe gun handling; parts; loading; shooting; cleaning; shooting from a standing position and shooting from a crossed stick position; and continued opportunities for skill development. Students will receive the Muzzleloading Rifle Handbook, NRA Gun Safety Rules brochure and completion certificate.
2.
Instructor Workshop for Teaching Muzzleloader Rifle Shooting
Note: This workshop will NOT include BIT as this was delivered in Spring for our Council.
For The Candidate, the time is a blend of instructional lecture, instructor role preparation and practical presentation coupled with range skill demonstrations. There will be multiple opportunities for the instructor candidates to practice these newly gained skills and role play as students for course mates then contribute to performance feedback sessions.
Budget Planning:
COST: $120 /   Combination Fee includes all days of instruction. (Basic + Instructor).  Scholarship funds may be available, contact Bud Harrelson for more information.
Current Scouter registration required - SYT must be up to date
.
Prices do not include fees associated with each discipline to be an Instructor or NRA membership.

What is National Youth Leadership Training?
The National Youth Leadership Training course was developed by the Boy Scouts of America to provide local councils with a standardized training course for the youth leadership of its Scouts BSA Troops, Crews, and Ships. This intensive week-long course is designed to parallel and complement the training that adult leaders receive in Wood Badge. Experience has shown that National Youth Leadership Training makes a positive difference in the lives of its graduates and in the operation of the units they lead.
What are the Requirements?
National Youth Leadership Training is not intended to be the initial training each youth leader receives. Each participant will need considerable experience in outdoor living skills, unit leadership, and the maturity to relate to the in-depth concepts presented in the Leadership Skills Area. Although the course is a lot of fun, it is physically and mentally demanding. For these reasons, participants will need to meet the following requirements:
Minimum Age of 13 with outstanding scout spirit and team-player attitude

Wilderness First Aid (WFA)
Cherokee Scout Reservation
3296 Boy Scout Camp Road
Yanceyville, NC
What is Wilderness First Aid?
Wilderness first aid, or “WFA," is a generic term that commonly refers to any training course that focuses on prevention, assessment, and treatment for an ill or injured person in a remote environment where definitive care by a physician and/or rapid transport is not readily available. This is defined as being an hour or more away from advanced care.  WFA courses are intended for anyone planning a remote adventure, from lay responders to medical professionals.
Why is WFA Important?
WFA prepares participants to identify and address medical issues that can arise in the backcountry.
This WFA course provides more advanced first aid beyond the lay responder level and provides information and teachs skills to respond to medical emergencies in the wild or other remote locations. It is important to remember that many providers offer “wilderness first aid” courses, but the courses vary in content, duration, and accreditation.  This course is an entry-level WFA course.
Treatment skills are important, but so is educating Scouts and adult leaders to recognize illnesses early and minimize the potential for injury.  WFA is not just for the backcountry.  It is just as relevant in urban areas during hurricanes, floods, fires, or mass casualty events when emergency services might be strained.  WFA knowledge can be lifesaving.
Who Needs WFA?
WFA is especially recommended for those planning and participating in activities where advanced medical care is delayed, backcountry camping trips, or high adventure trips.
It is appropriate for Cub Scout, Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scout unit leaders to participate in the WFA course.
Scouts ages 14 and up are invited to participate in the WFA course. Youth participants should understand this course can be challenging and should only be undertaken if able to stay focused for long periods in all kinds of weather conditions.
When youth participate, BSA youth protection policies must be followed.
It is recommended that youth register as buddy pairs of the same gender and with no more than a two years age difference.
When female youth participate, the female Scout's family and/or unit is responsible for providing female adult supervision.
How Does the Old North State Council Offer WFA?
A BSA-led task force developed a 16-hour WFA training curriculum specifically for Scouts and Scouters to help them provide assessment and treatment miles from advanced care. The Old North State Council partners with Emergency Care and Safety Institute (ECSI) to offer the BSA-approved WFA curriculum.
The course you are taking is a BSA-approved hybrid WFA course provided by ECSI. Part 1 consists of 8 hours of online study. Part 2 is a skills assessment that tests your ability to apply the knowledge gained in the online portion through group scenarios. Part 2, which is face-to-face, is a minimum of 8 hours in duration, not counting meals and breaks.
When Will I Receive Information about completing the online portion of the WFA course?
Participants will receive an email 3-4 weeks prior to the face-to-face skills assessment with directions on how to complete the online portion of the WFA course. This email will also include information and instructions on preparing for your day at camp.  If you do not receive the email in that time frame, please contact Nita Grubbs, nita.grubbs@scouting.org.

/081-BALOOHSR.desc:
BASIC ADULT LEADER OUTDOOR ORIENTATION (BALOO):
This course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for those leaders who are interested in adding a camping component to their Den or Pack activities.
Who should take BALOO?
Scouting America requires that you have at least one BALOO-trained adult on every Cub Scout Den or Pack overnight outdoor event.
A BALOO-trained leader should be at any overnighter regardless of whether it is a Pack, District or Council event.
Having at least one BALOO-trained adult will make your Cub Scouts’ camping experience as awesome as it can be; but more is even better!
Why should I take BALOO?
Leaders who complete BALOO training are better prepared to plan pack den or pack overnight events.
You’ll learn how to make camping activities and outings fun. You’ll discover how to keep your Cub Scouts safe and entertained. And you’ll learn how to plan an event that’s rooted firmly in Cub Scouting’s principles.
Successful experiences in the outdoors make Cub Scouts — and their parents — more likely to keep coming back.
How do I take BALOO?
BALOO consists of two components: online and hands-on. You’ll need to complete both — in order — to qualify as a “Trained” Cub Scout outdoor leader.
Online component:
The online portion of BALOO is available 24/7 on the Scouting America Learn Center. The goal of the online portion is to make the best use of time to allow leaders to experience as much as possible during the practical hands-on training.  The online training contains introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the practical training.  If you do not present your BALOO online training certificate, they still will have you take part in the BALOO Training, but your training will not be entered as complete.  To take the Prerequisite go to
https://my.scouting.org/
Click on these:
Scouting America Learn Center
Expanded Learning
BALOO
BALOO Prerequisite Training
Add Plan
My Learning
Please bring a copy of your BALOO Prerequisite Training completion certificate to the Training.
Practical, hands-on component:
In this 1.5-day course, Scouting America's Cub Scout level camping policies will be taught along with the necessary tools to help Packs and Dens carry out a successful camping experience.  Completion of this course is mandatory for at least one adult on a Pack overnighter.

/081-IOLSHSRFALL.desc:
INTRODUCTION TO OUTDOOR LEADER SKILLS (IOLS):
The Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills course builds and expands on the concepts and themes introduced in Position-Specific Training and provides Scouters with the confidence to take youth into the outdoors.
Specifically, this hands-on program gives adult leaders a practical introduction to the Patrol Method of a youth-led Troop by teaching many of the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the out-of-doors. In addition, the teaching methods, activities, and games model the variety of teaching used in effective and engaging Scouting programs.
Hands-on participation is the best learning tool, and this course models the techniques used by effective Scoutmasters, Advisors, and other leaders in the Scouting program. Attendees will see and experience different aspects of how Scouting works while playing the role of Scouts in a Troop.
Participants should leave the training experience with a full understanding of how the Patrol Method operates, a feeling of comfort in working with and instructing their Scouts, and an increased level of confidence taking Scouts outdoors safely. With that comes great satisfaction.
IOLS is a required course for Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters to be considered fully trained in their positions and earn their Trained patch. (Online or classroom position-specific training and current Hazardous Weather Training complete the requirements to be fully position trained and earn the Trained patch.)

/081-NYLT.desc:
Leadership is a key factor in the development of a Scout. One of the most valuable things Scouting offers a scout is the opportunity to be a leader and to develop their leadership skills. The National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) course provides an exceptional opportunity to do just that.
NYLT is an intensive six-day training experience for Senior Patrol Leaders, Assistant Senior Patrol Leaders, Patrol Leaders, Crew Leaders, and other youth leaders as well as prospective Troop/Crew leaders. The course uses a systematic approach to teach contemporary leadership skills, with an emphasis on both theory and practical application in a Scouting context. For the Scout who desires to be a better and more effective leader, NYLT is an unparalleled opportunity.
Dates:
December 27, 2027 to January 1, 2028
Location:
Henson Scout Reservation, 5700 Nanticoke RD, Rhodesdale, MD
Cost:
$275
per participant. A
$305
late fee will apply if not paid in full on or before September 25, 2027.
Eligibility:
A Scout must be at least 13 years of age or have completed the seventh grade and under the age of 18 if a Scout or under the age of 21 if a Venturer. A Scout must also hold at least the rank of First Class, be currently registered in a Scouts BSA Troop or Venturing Crew. All participants must have a recommendation from their unit leader. Completion of Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troop/Crews is a helpful start. Because NYLT is an intensive training experience, participants should possess sufficient maturity, judgment, and leadership potential to successfully complete the program.
Equipment & Supplies:
Your regular field uniform is the official uniform of NYLT. Participants need to bring their normal camping gear, including a tent for each individual participant. Participants will receive a detailed equipment list one month prior to the start of the course. Fees include all meals, NYLT swag, resource guide, and upon successful course completion, a patch and certificate of completion.
Health & Safety:

/081-WFA.desc:
ECSI Wilderness First Aid Course
The 2027 ECSI Wilderness First Aid Course is a two part course consisting of an 8-hour online section which must be completed prior to the practical skills course. Both the online course and in-person practical skills course must be completed in order to earn the WFA certification. You will receive a completion card that will be valid for two years.
Wilderness First Aid (WFA) is the assessment of and treatment given to an ill or injured person in a remote environment where definitive care of a physician and/or rapid transport is not readily available.
Time is the major element distinguishing Wilderness First Aid from Standard First Aid.  When calling 911 is not an immediate option, or when help is hours or even days away, the task of treating the ill or injured can challenge your "standard" first aid skills.  Heat, cold, rain, wind, darkness, and distance over land or water may separate you from definitive care and evacuation may also need to be improvised from what is available. Communication with the "outside world" may be limited or unavailable.  All of these things may very well be part of the WFA world.
The course is for those who plan trips to remote areas far from "normal" EMS Services, providing hands-on skills practice for the remote site.
Wilderness First Aid is required at each B.S.A high-adventure location. Check the particular locations for specific requirements and exceptions.

/081-asrbaloo.desc:
BASIC ADULT LEADER OUTDOOR ORIENTATION (BALOO):
This course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for those leaders who are interested in adding a camping component to their Den or Pack activities.
Who should take BALOO?
Scouting America requires that you have at least one BALOO-trained adult on every Cub Scout Den or Pack overnight outdoor event.
A BALOO-trained leader should be at any overnighter regardless of whether it is a Pack, District or Council event.
Having at least one BALOO-trained adult will make your Cub Scouts’ camping experience as awesome as it can be; but more is even better!
Why should I take BALOO?
Leaders who complete BALOO training are better prepared to plan pack den or pack overnight events.
You’ll learn how to make camping activities and outings fun. You’ll discover how to keep your Cub Scouts safe and entertained. And you’ll learn how to plan an event that’s rooted firmly in Cub Scouting’s principles.
Successful experiences in the outdoors make Cub Scouts — and their parents — more likely to keep coming back.
How do I take BALOO?
BALOO consists of two components: online and hands-on. You’ll need to complete both — in order — to qualify as a “Trained” Cub Scout outdoor leader.
Online component:
The online portion of BALOO is available 24/7 on the Scouting America Learn Center. The goal of the online portion is to make the best use of time to allow leaders to experience as much as possible during the practical hands-on training.  The online training contains introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the practical training.  If you do not present your BALOO online training certificate, they still will have you take part in the BALOO Training, but your training will not be entered as complete.  To take the Prerequisite go to
https://my.scouting.org/
Click on these:
Scouting America Learn Center
Expanded Learning
BALOO
BALOO Prerequisite Training

Please bring a copy of your BALOO Prerequisite Training completion certificate to the Training.
Practical, hands-on component:
In this 1.5-day course, Scouting America's Cub Scout level camping policies will be taught along with the necessary tools to help Packs and Dens carry out a successful camping experience.  Completion of this course is mandatory for at least one adult on a Pack overnighter.

/081-hsrIOLSspring.desc:
INTRODUCTION TO OUTDOOR LEADER SKILLS (IOLS):
The Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills course builds and expands on the concepts and themes introduced in Position-Specific Training and provides Scouters with the confidence to take youth into the outdoors.
Specifically, this hands-on program gives adult leaders a practical introduction to the Patrol Method of a youth-led Troop by teaching many of the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the out-of-doors. In addition, the teaching methods, activities, and games model the variety of teaching used in effective and engaging Scouting programs.
Hands-on participation is the best learning tool, and this course models the techniques used by effective Scoutmasters, Advisors, and other leaders in the Scouting program. Attendees will see and experience different aspects of how Scouting works while playing the role of Scouts in a Troop.
Participants should leave the training experience with a full understanding of how the Patrol Method operates, a feeling of comfort in working with and instructing their Scouts, and an increased level of confidence taking Scouts outdoors safely. With that comes great satisfaction.
IOLS is a required course for Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters to be considered fully trained in their positions and earn their Trained patch. (Online or classroom position-specific training and current Hazardous Weather Training complete the requirements to be fully position trained and earn the Trained patch.)

EVENT DETAILS
Do you train leaders, parents, or scouts? Have you considered training but don’t know where to begin? Or maybe you have years of experience in training but want to add some pizzazz to it.
Come join us for The Fundamentals Part 1: Science of Training and Fundamentals Part 2: Craft of Training and learn about the science and art of training others.
The Fundamentals Part 1: Science of Training session is designed to help scouters, regardless of their experience, to present effective training. It will also help those who might have trained for other organizations learn Scouting America's training techniques and it will help freshen up the skills of current Scouting America trainers.
The Fundamentals Part 2: Craft of Training session is designed to provide and help platform skills of the trainer with the focus in raising the level of the trainer’s skill. In this session you will have the opportunity to apply strategies for managing learner behaviors, giving and receiving feedback, and practice training methodologies.
At the conclusion of the training, you will be able to understand the principles of how people learn and equip yourself with a broad range of ideas, techniques, and materials, which will enable you to select approaches to communicate your messages most successfully, and with PIZZAZZ!
The Fundamentals Part 2: Craft of Training emphasizes the importance of “experiential learning,” or learning by doing, as well as numerous other contemporary training strategies. These strategies can then be applied to a wide range of training programs.

Learn to Play Chess
Open to Scouts of all ages!  Do you want to learn how to play chess?  We’ll teach you the rules of chess and the basic ideas behind the game.  It’s not as difficult to learn how to play as you might think.  “Every chess master was once a beginner,” said chess master and author Irving Chernev; and once you know how to play, there is a lifetime of discovery and fun ahead of you as you learn to play better.
In this session we’ll cover:
How to Play Chess – the Rules of the Game
Basic Checkmates
Basic Combinations
How to Start a Chess Game
Play Chess – everyone gets to play a game!
Fees:
The cost is $10.00 per Scout.
What to Bring:
Each Scout should wear the field uniform. A responsible adult must be on site throughout the tournament.  Chess sets will be provided so please do not bring one.
When and Where:
Saturday, November 21, 2026, 1-5 PM
Marriott Scout Service Center
9190 Rockville Pike
Bethesda, MD 20814
Play Chess Better
Open to chess-playing Scouts of all ages!  To attend, you must know the rules of chess and have previously played a game of chess.  Do you play chess but don’t know where to start when it comes to deciding which piece to move and where?  We’ll cover winning chess principles, what to look for on the chessboard, and how to come up with a plan.  “Strategy requires thought, tactics require observation,” said chess grandmaster and world champion Max Euwe.
In this session we’ll cover:
Opening Principles and the Common Openings
Endgame Principles
Advanced Combinations
Elements of Strategy
Solving Chess Problems
We’ll also talk about the chess merit badge and invite you to start earning it, if you have not done so already.
Fees:  The cost is $10.00 per Scout.
What to Bring:  Each Scout should wear the field uniform. A responsible adult must be on site throughout the tournament.  Chess sets will be provided so please do not bring one.

Event Overview
NCAC STEM is hosting an event for Scouts BSA to earn the Engineering Merit Badge on Saturday, Novermber 7 2026
They will host the event at Sally's STEM Shack at Camp William B. Snyder, Haymarket, VA.
Who can attend?
Scouts BSA.
Class Overview
Engineers turn ideas into reality. For example, they will take the plans drawn on paper for an exciting new roller coaster—a design with loops, drops, and corkscrews—and figure out how to build it so that it will be fast, safe to ride, and affordable to build. Engineers devise all sorts of things, ranging from a tiny, low-cost battery for your cellphone to a gigantic dam.  Come spend a day learning about the fun of being an engineer!
Event Schedule
The session will run from 9 AM to 3 PM
Prerequisites
Requirements #1, 2, and 9 are prerequisites.
Event Requirements and Details
Uniforms: SBSA should wear Class B uniform.
What to bring with you on November 7th:
Blue card filled out and signed by your SM
Pencil and notebook
Water bottle/lunch/snacks
Directions and Parking
: Camp William B. Snyder is located at 6100 Antioch Road, Haymarket, VA 20169. See attached map for directions to Sally’s STEM Shack. Parking is available to the right of the building.
Registration Fee:
Early Bird registration (deadline October 28), $25; Regular registration (deadline November 2), $30; Late registration (deadline November 7) $35.

Scouts who have completed their unit’s introduction to leadership course, have been practicing these skills, and are ready for the next level of training should attend NYLT once they meet all Eligibility Requirements.
NYLT ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS
Scouts must:
Complete their home Unit’s Introduction to Leadership Skills course*
Receive approval from your Scoutmaster or Unit leader
Be at least 13 years of age by course start date
Earn First Class rank, if registered in a Troop
Have current BSA Health Form (Parts A, B, and C)
Be comfortable camping and cooking outdoors
Commit to attending the entire six-day course
* Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops (ILST), Crews (ILSC), and Ships (ILSS) should be offered through a Scout’s home unit. Ask your Unit Leader how you can participate in this course.

REFUND POLICY
Cancel within 3 days of making a registration and the entire amount is returned.
After 3 days of making the registration but not within 14 of the event the customer is charged 15% of the registration cost being cancelled.
Once within 14 days of the event the customer is charged 100% of the registration cost being cancelled.
Fees cannot be credited toward another event. This policy is true for any event with fees over $25.00 per participant/registrant unless stated otherwise.
WHAT NYLT IS (AND IS NOT)
NYLT is not like summer camp and is not designed for rank advancement or earning merit badges.  NYLT is an intense and challenging hands-on leadership training program.  It is essential that NYLT participants be physically, emotionally, and mentally prepared to handle the demands of this advanced training. In order to get the most benefit from this unique experience, participants must exhibit emotional maturity, a positive attitude, proficiency in basic camping and outdoor cooking, and have an ambition to serve in leadership roles.
Behavior at NYLT: Participants agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the Scout Oath and Law.
Scholarship requests can be completed during the registration.

/082-2027ScoutOrienteering.desc:
Test out your troop or crew member's navigation skills at this exciting map and compass competition. Scouts and Crew members with compete in age groups and different course levels in the morning as individuals. The afternoon event is designed around competing as a unit (Troop or Crew) to gather the greatest score than the other scouting units. This event is open to all Scouts BSA Troops, Venturing Crews, and other appropriately aged Scouting groups; minimum age for this event is 10 and a half years old.
REGISTRATION IS REQUIRED
-- Please be aware that your unit must register online to take part in this event. There is no walk in registration for any unit or scout. Adjustments to the number of members from a unit can be made on the day of the event, but refunds may not be given. A unit is defined as at least two scouts and two registered adult leaders.
Summary:
This event is open to all ScoutsBSA Troops, GSUSA units (ages 10 and up) and Venturing Crews. Scouts will be paired up (buddy system applies) and compete for awards to be presented to the first 10 places in each event. The morning sessions will include: instruction Orienteering course for Scouts new to the sport, competitions in one of four levels of orienteering courses, and other skill-building competitive events. Each Scout pair will have an opportunity to choose two events in the morning. We strongly recommend instruction take place at a unit level prior to your arrival. The instructional Orienteering course is a "no compete, no awards" hands on teaching course that your scouts can learn by using the Teaching EDGE method to learn the art of Orienteering. To ensure fairness, competition will also be broken into two age groups for most events in the morning, under 14 years of age and Scouts 14 years of age or older. Venturing Crews with members over 18 years old may be scored as a third grouping based on judging decision on the day of the event. After a brief break at 1pm, the afternoon event will be a 90-minute Orienteering score course. The afternoon event is a unit based competition with youth leadership taking charge of their units in planning and directing their teams. The event will be completed with awards from the morning events at 5:00 pm.
Cost is $12 per youth and includes an event patch for all youth participants. Adults may purchase patches at cost on the day of the event pending availability.
This event is run with volunteers from and supported by the NCAC and has the added experienced of help from the
Quantico Orienteering Club
.
Buddy system is strictly enforced with all events and adults are not permit "in the woods” during the competitions.* The morning competition will be on the individual (scout) pair level and on the unit level. Each troop or crew unit will have a unit score from this event based on the average of the unit's top five pairs from that unit.
Camping will be available on both Friday and Saturday nights. The cost is $2 per person per night and can be completed as part of your unit registration. We will assign locations for your troop or crew to camp in the open area within walking distance of the event start and registration area. Please be aware that participant's cars may need to be relocated to the main park area to allow enough space for other scouting units to set up their camp site.
This event is restricted to Scout Troops and Venture Crews only:
Because of the large volume of Scouts attending this event and the level of competition, we cannot accommodate Cub Scouts or Webelos at this event. The youth must be registered member of a Troop, Team, Ship or Crew.

This in-person course will cover all the Cub leader and committee positions, to include assistant positions, in a seminar setting: Cubmaster; Den Leader; and Pack Committee.  All the material in the online courses will be covered plus how to actually perform your duties and be a great leader, right from the start.  There will be lots of tips and resources not covered in the online courses, and time for discussion. There may be a few silly jokes.
You will come away with an understanding of Scouting and the Cub program that you cannot get online, with practical tips on how to organize and lead Cubs, how to organize and run meetings, and how to handle the pack admin/back office requirements.
Should you just take the four hour online course in my.scouting instead of this in-person course?  The online course covers the bare minimum but you could call yourself trained if you pass the multiple choice tests.  However, if you truly want to Do Your Best, and be the best possible leader you can be from your first day as a leader, and lead and inspire youth, you'll take this in-person course even if you've already taken the online course.
The fee covers the NCAC direct and indirect costs and you'll take home all the course materials and resources in a binder ($3.71); a Trained patch (which would be $1.99 at the Scout Shop); and some useful items you can use as the genius Cub leader that the course will train you to become.
If the fee is an obstacle, contact the course director (
joepallone@verizon.net
) and this will be handled confidentially.

and typically ends by 12:30.  Wear your uniform.  Bring a pen and your own beverages and snacks (this keeps costs down).  A Keurig machine is available but you should bring your own mug, K-pods, sweetener, cream, etc.  Walk-ins are welcome but we can't guarantee we'll have enough course materials on hand.
Do Your Best.  See you then.
