/083-WoodBadgeSpringCourse1683271.desc:
Central Florida Council
Wood Badge "Spring Course 16-83-27-1
Course Information:
Wood Badge  Orientation:January 30, 2027 (Virtual via ZOOM call 3:00 - 4:30 pm).
Weekend 1: February 12-14, 2027
Weekend 2: February 27-28, 2027
Course Director, Mike Carlo
What Is Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is the Super Bowl of adult leadership training! Baden-Powell began Wood Badge in 1919 as a way to ensure that the leaders of packs and troops were properly trained. Since then, Wood Badge has been held worldwide, providing advanced leadership training to thousands of Scout leaders.
Wood Badge builds upon the best traditions and experiences of Scouting America. It draws from a wide range of courses within and beyond the bounds of Scouting to present the latest in leadership theory and team development. It reflects the best of over a century of Scouting experience.
Wood Badge draws upon current leadership models used by Corporate America, academic circles, and successful organizations throughout the country, with some common sense thrown in for clarity.
Who Should Attend Wood Badge?
YOU!
As an adult Scouter, you should attend Wood Badge.
Wood Badge is designed to meet the advanced leadership needs of all Scouters. It is for unit-level Scouters, such as Cub leaders, Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters, Venturing Crew Advisors, Committee Chairs, and Committee Members. Scouters serving at the district and council levels can also achieve greater effectiveness through Wood Badge.
Remember, every Scout deserves a trained leader!
To attend a Wood Badge course, individuals must:
Be registered members of Scouting America. (Youth 18 and older may attend as long as the appropriate Safeguarding our youth guidelines are followed. They do not need to be registered in an adult leadership role.)
Have completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment. All participants are required to complete the Annual Health and Medical Record form.
Why Attend?
By taking Wood Badge, Scouters will acquire invaluable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning, and leading change. Participants will learn to better understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our Scouting communities. They will learn skills that will make them better leaders.
Wood Badge-trained leaders are able to deliver and improve programs and create a more meaningful experience for all the youth Scouting serves.
Participants will internalize the five themes of Wood Badge:
Living the Values
Growing
Connecting
Guiding
Empowering

/089-NYLT23.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops, crews, or ships, and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what he or she must KNOW, and what he or she must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the Scouts, Venturers, and Sea Scouts go on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership. National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is a coed six-day course, staffed primarily by youth NYLT alumni.
Classes are held in an outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ the leadership skills much faster. Please note: the BSA-created curriculum includes a realistic simulation of a first aid event. Scouts should Be Prepared to learn how to provide aid in a real-life situation.
Who can attend
To participate, you must be a registered member of the BSA at least 13 years old,

Experience the Adventure at Camp Frank G. Lumpkin!
Session 1: June 14–20, 2026
Session 2: June 21–27, 2026
Get ready for the ultimate Scouting adventure of the summer at Camp Frank G. Lumpkin (FGL) — where fun, friendship, and the great outdoors come together on the shores of beautiful West Point Lake! Summer camp is the highlight of every Scout’s year, and there’s no better place to make memories than at FGL — the premier freshwater aquatics base in the Southeast.
Nestled on a 900-acre peninsula between Atlanta and Birmingham, Camp FGL offers everything Scouts dream about — from kayaking, canoeing, motorboating, and jet skiing on the McKenzie Waterfront, to the thrill of our 50-foot climbing and rappelling tower, archery and shooting ranges, and over 80 unique merit badges and specialty programs to choose from. Scouts can dive into STEM adventures, ecology exploration, and hands-on crafts while building skills and confidence that last a lifetime.
Our Chattahoochee Council staff and volunteers are passionate about providing a top-quality program, ensuring your unit’s week is filled with fun, fellowship, and unforgettable experiences. Whether it’s relaxing by the lake, tackling COPE challenges, or cheering at evening campfires, Camp FGL promises something special for everyone.
So grab your gear, rally your troop, and join us at Camp Frank G. Lumpkin in 2026 for a week of adventure, learning, and pure Scouting fun.
Because at FGL — adventure isn’t just part of camp, it’s a way of life!

NYLT is a six-day advanced leadership course designed to teach Scouts the tools, techniques, and skills they need to be better leaders – not only in their units, but also at home, in school, and in their daily lives. Led by an exemplary, highly-trained youth staff, NYLT participants work hard and play hard together through group activities, games, and adventures as they experience Scouting at its best.
Who can go to NYLT?
Scouts and Venturers can attend NYLT if they meet these nationally-mandated requirements before the start of the course.
Scouts BSA: Age 13 or older / At least First Class rank / Attended ILST
Venturing/Sea Scouts: Age 14 or be age 13 and have completed the 8th grade / Attended ILSC/ILSS

Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops (ILST)
This workshop teaches youth leaders about their leadership role and how to most effectively achieve success in that role.  It also teaches about collaboration, communication, and preparation. This is a prerequisite for all Scouts who plan to attend NYLT (National Youth Leadership Training). This course may be taught in the unit by the Scoutmaster or by District and Council Trainers.

Why attend National Youth Leadership Training?
Scouts
In your Scouting career, you will get many opportunities to lead your fellow Scouts through activities, projects, and outings as you advance. How can you make sure you have the skills you need to lead them to success?
NYLT can teach you what you will need to become a better leader. At NYLT, you will learn how to communicate effectively, how to resolve conflicts, and how to work towards a vision. You will work as part of a patrol with your fellow participants, practicing your Scouting skills and growing together as a team. And you will have fun along the way, with games and interactive activities that reinforce different leadership techniques.
NYLT is staffed by Scouts like yourself who have gone through the program and spent months in preparation to teach the course. They will guide you and your patrol through your six days at NYLT, and they make sure that NYLT is not just about teaching you leadership skills, but about giving you a leadership experience that you will never forget. You will be able to take home Scout skills, games, songs, and practices that will make your unit even better. And you might even find that your six days at NYLT is a time of self-discovery, as you set a personal vision and learn how to set goals to fulfill it.
Leaders
National Youth Leadership Training will bring new skills and greater enthusiasm to your youth leadership.
Scouting recognizes that unit leaders have primary responsibility for training their youth leaders. NYLT is designed to support that role by helping Scouts develop critical leadership skills such as setting goals, communicating with others, and team development.
Using the Patrol Method as a framework for teaching, an NYLT course is not only ideal for training youth leaders at every level, but it can also be a valuable experience for older Scouts and Venturers.

/092-conservationweekend.desc:
Join us for a weekend event dedicated to conservation and learning.
The 2026 Conservation Weekend will be held from November 13 - 15
at Camp Woodruff
.
This weekend offers something for every scout. There are 3 sessions available to fill with your choice of 19 Merit Badges, conservation projects and other trainings. All sessions will be staffed by dynamic instructors that are experts in their field. Some sessions will fill up faster than others, so register today!  This event also includes a conservation themed workshop Saturday evening with games and information that will end in a fun cracker barrel for everyone.
Registration is OPEN!
Need help with registration?
New!
Angling Educator
Angling Educator is a national course taught by a BSA Certified Angling Instructor. Angling Educators learn age-based and skills-appropriate fishing tools and techniques for simple cane pole and spin cast fishing. It prepares leaders to teach fishing skills, and plan and run fishing events for their troop, district, or council.
New!
Earth Tribe Challenge
The Earth Tribe is a global community of young people who are passionate about the environment and actively engaged as a global citizens to preserve and protect our planet.  The Earth Tribe guides young people on an educational journey to develop the awareness, competencies and leadership skills necessary to create environmental change in their communities.  Through a series of exciting Earth Tribe Challenges, young people learn how to connect with nature, become champions for sustainability, and engage in taking action for the environment.  To be a member of the Earth Tribe is a personal commitment to improve the health of the planet and make the world a better place.
Conservation Service Project – Tools & Trails
The Conservation Service Tools & Trails program builds on the Conservation Service Project with a focus specifically on the tools used for trial maintenance and upkeep. Scouts and Adults will be instructed on ethical use of conservation tools like the pickax; spade; bow saw; cross-cut saw; loppers; McLeod, and Pulaski. Then, participants will put their new skills to work on Woodruff’s trails. Scouts fully participating in this 3-hour session may complete the National Outdoor Award Conservation Segment Requirement #2.
Conservation Service Project
The Conservation Service Project is a 3-hour project slot for completing conservation-related service projects at Woodruff. Scouts and Adults will have the opportunity to participate in projects like clearing invasive species; treating hemlocks for disease; updating the forestry trail installed in 2022; planting new trees, and other opportunities. Scouts and Adults are welcome to sign up for more than one project time slot.
Conservation Scout Skills
The Conservation Scout Skills program is specifically for those Scouts who are new to Scouts BSA, or who have limited experience with conservation skills. Basic Scout Skills related to conservation form the basis of the program. Scouts will be instructed and have hands-on opportunities related to the Scout – First Class rank requirements in Outdoor Code, Leave No Trace principals, low-impact camping, environmental issues, identification of poisonous or hazardous plants, signs of wildlife, and more.
Instructions to Get Merit Badge Reports
Conservation and Scouting America have been partners for a long time. Camping, hiking, and respect for the outdoors are a part of the Scouting heritage. Many of the requirements for advancement from Tenderfoot through Eagle Scout rank call for an increasing awareness and understanding of the natural sciences. Many former Scouts have become leaders in conserving our environment and protecting it from abuse. Right now Scouts are involved in learning about environmental problems and actively working to make a difference.
Age Restrictions
All Scouts BSA registered Scouts are eligible to attend Conservation Weekend. We recommend that Scouts not attending with their troop

/092-universityofscouting.desc:
University of Scouting
Learn More. Lead Better. Scout Stronger.
Join fellow Scouting volunteers and youth leaders for a day of learning, sharing ideas, and discovering new ways to deliver an outstanding Scouting experience.
Discover new ways to make Scouting better
The University of Scouting is a one-day supplemental training event hosted by the Atlanta Area Council, Scouting America. It brings together Scouting volunteers, parents, and youth leaders for a day of education, collaboration, and practical program development.
Whether you are a new volunteer learning the basics or an experienced leader looking for fresh ideas, University of Scouting offers opportunities to strengthen your skills, connect with fellow Scouters, and bring new energy to your unit.
Cost:
$20 (includes lunch and patch)
Date:
February 20, 2027
Location:
SCAD University
Address:
1600 Peachtree St NE, Atlanta, GA 30309
UoS 2027 Catalog Coming Soon
Who should attend?
University of Scouting welcomes participants from across the Scouting program, including:
Cub Scout Leaders
Explore ways to plan engaging den and pack meetings, support advancement, and create fun, memorable experiences for Cub Scouts.
Scouts BSA Leaders
Build skills in troop leadership, outdoor programming, advancement, and youth-led activities.
Committee Members and Unit Volunteers
Learn practical approaches to unit administration, recruiting, fundraising, and supporting your unit's leadership team.
Venturing Advisors and Youth Leaders
Discover leadership techniques, program ideas, and opportunities to help youth take ownership of their Scouting experience.
What can you learn?
University of Scouting offers a variety of supplemental training opportunities, from foundational leadership topics to more advanced sessions. Course offerings may vary each year.
Leadership development:
Strengthen your ability to mentor, guide, and support youth.
Program planning:
Discover activities and resources that make unit meetings and events more engaging.
Advancement and skills:
Learn strategies for helping Scouts progress and develop new abilities.
Unit management:
Explore ways to improve communication, organization, recruitment, and volunteer involvement.
Networking and collaboration:
Share experiences and learn from other volunteers throughout the Atlanta Area Council.
Make the most of your day
Review the course catalog
: Explore the available classes and select sessions that fit your role, interests, and unit's needs.
Connect with other Scouters
: Meet volunteers from other units and districts, exchange ideas, and build relationships that strengthen Scouting.
Bring what you learn back to your unit:
Put new knowledge, resources, and inspiration into practice to create a better experience for every Scout.
Get involved as an instructor or volunteer
Have a skill, experience, or idea that could benefit other Scouters? University of Scouting also provides opportunities for volunteers to contribute as instructors, event volunteers, and exhibitors.
Sharing your knowledge helps fellow leaders grow and strengthens Scouting throughout the Atlanta Area Council.
Ready to take your Scouting skills to the next level?
Make plans to join fellow volunteers and youth leaders at University of Scouting. Invest in your development, discover fresh ideas, and help the Atlanta Area Council deliver meaningful Scouting adventures for every youth.

/095-121595.desc:
Wilderness First Aid Certification Course
May 1-2, 2027
Flint River Council 100-year Anniversary
WFA Certification Course for Adult Leaders
8:00 a.m. Saturday to 2:00 p.m. Sunday
Camp Thunder at Gerald I. Lawhorn Scouting Base
WFA certification is required for all adult leaders attending BSA high adventure camps
--------------------------------------------
Certified Wilderness First Aid instructors Dr. Susan Northrup, M.D., and David McLaughlin, WFR, will lead a team of instructors through 20 hours of informative and intense training at Camp Thunder.
Course curriculum includes patient assessment; symptoms, treatments, and evacuation guidelines for chest injuries, shock, head and spine injuries, bone and joint injuries, wounds and infections, and other medical emergencies; first aid kits; and “hands on” skill scenarios.
Course attendees will spend approximately half of the course in classroom instruction and half of the course practicing skills in a wilderness setting.
Course attendees will leave with two-year WFA certification and the competence to recognize and treat injuries and medical emergencies in the wilderness.
Course attendees will sleep in platform tents Saturday night at Camp Thunder.  Two Saturday meals, two Sunday meals, and snacks throughout the weekend will be provided.  Course attendees who wish to arrive Friday evening may arrive after 7:00 p.m. and sleep in a platform tent.
The course tuition will cover lodging and meals; course training book (Wilderness First Aid: Emergency Care in Remote Locations); NOLS Wilderness Medicine Field Guide; and training materials.
In order to be WFA certified, current CPR certification is required.  An optional CPR certification training will take place Sunday after lunch following the completion of WFA.  Participants not taking the optional CPR certification must provide proof of current CPR certification at the beginning of the WFA in order to become WFA certified.  It is highly recommended that course attendees take CPR during the WFA weekend to avoid a lapse in WFA certification following the expiration of an existing CPR certification.
The course will be limited to 30 adult leaders, so please sign up immediately.  A limited number of qualified Scouts may be accepted into the course.  Please contact David McLaughlin if you have an interested Scout.
Please contact David McLaughlin at mclaughlin247@gmail.com if you have any questions about the course.

Camp Thunder presents the winter adventure: WINTER CAMP 2026: LEGEND ON THE YETI
Nestled between the pristine Flint River and historic Pine Mountain in Georgia, Winter Camp 2026 is a new brand of winter camp — and this year, something else is out there with us.
Locals have talked about it for generations: broad tracks in the frost along the river bottom, a shape moving through the pines at the edge of the firelight, a sound that isn't a coyote. Most folks laugh it off. Then they spend a December night at Camp Thunder.
Winter Camp 2026: Legend on the Yeti brings Scouts together for four days of merit badges, brotherhood, and cold-weather adventure — wrapped in a camp-wide legend that unfolds a little more each night. Track it. Test yourself against it. Earn your place in the story.
THE LEGEND
Every night of camp, another piece of the legend comes to light — a discovered artifact, a rangers' report, an eyewitness account. Troops collect evidence across the week, and the units that put the pieces together first are honored at the closing campfire.
DATES
December 19 – December 22
Daily schedule subject to change.
ADULT REGISTRATION — IMPORTANT
ALL adults who are camping must provide the camping department with their BSA Membership ID by December 15, 2024. Failure to provide this information will result in those adults not being able to camp with his or her troop.
BSA national policy states that ALL adults or parents who are camping for longer than 72 hours must be a registered member with Scouts and possess current Youth Protection Training.
CALLING ALL MERIT BADGE COUNSELORS
Winter Camp runs on the adults who step up to teach. Merit badges are the heart of this week, and we need counselors to make the schedule happen — your expertise is what turns a class into an experience a Scout remembers.
Teach a merit badge, camp free. Any adult who serves as a merit badge counselor for the week attends Winter Camp 2026 at no cost — your fee is waived entirely, and the slot does not count against your troop's two free adults.
How it works: Review the merit badges offered at Winter Camp in the program guide, pick the badge or badges you're able to teach, and let us know. We'll handle the classroom, the schedule, and the Scouts — you bring the expertise.
Interested? Reach out to Greg Joiner for further information and to claim your badge:
Email: greg.joiner@scouting.org
Phone: 762-247-0900
Counselor slots are filled as they're claimed, so reach out early to lock in the badge you want.
CAMP FEES

Adults: 2 free per troop (with a minimum of 5 youth)
Additional adults: $85.00 each
MERIT BADGES

/095-FRCWoodBadge2027.desc:
Flint River Council
Wood Badge
is BACK and happening in 2027!!
Wood Badge is open to all adults and will be a memorable and fun training experience that will change your life!
History of the Wood Badge
In 1919, Baden-Powell introduced a standardised training system for leaders. Scouts who successfully completed the leader training were awarded a Wood Badge. Made of two wooden beads worn at the end of a leather lace, the first bead came from the ceremonial necklace of Zulu Chief Dinizulu, while the second was carved by the recipient.
In 1987, four Wood Badge beads were given to Dinizulu’s grandson as a symbolic act of returning the beads to their rightful heirs.
Today, the tradition of the Wood Badge continues with leaders receiving beads made from acacia wood. Leaders are also enrolled as members of the 1st Gilwell Park Scout Group - where the first Wood Badges were given out in 1919 -, and can wear the distinctive Gilwell scarf and woggle.

/127-115814.desc:
Wilderness First Aid Certification Classes
Emergency Care in Remote Locations, this course provides information on how to handle common injuries and illnesses when medical care is an hour away or more. This class will teach you what to look for and what to do in the event of an emergency, and direct you to the most appropriate type of care.
This class includes
Expanded information on heat and cold emergencies
Updated guidelines for managing snake bite emergencies
New information on managing diabetic emergencies
Skill sheets providing step-by-step visual reviews of procedures discussed
Flow charts reinforcing the decision-making process and appropriate procedures
Decision tables provide a concise summary of what signs first aiders should look for and what treatment steps they should take
All participants in The Wilderness First Aid class should be at least 16 years old. The course is taught at an adult pace and some portions involve treatment and decisions that can be emotionally and physically distressing. The Course Director is authorized to make exceptions. Please contact the Course Director directly prior to registering any youth under 16.
Be prepared to spend some time outdoors during this course. Practice sessions are hands-on.
Lunch will be provided. Please contact the Course Director with any dietary needs.
Attendees must attend both Saturday and Sunday classes to complete training.  This not an overnight event. Classes will start and end each day and participants must be present and on time for both sessions.
A current CPR/AED certification is required for the Wilderness First Aid Certification.  CPR/AED is not taught during this class.  If you do not have a current CPR/AED certification you can sign up for a class at the links below.

Okpik 2027 - 2028
Cold Weather Outdoor Training
Okpik (Ook’pick) is the Inuit name for a Snowy Owl. The Okpik course aims to provide participants with the skills and knowledge to enjoy an outdoor experience in cold weather; to help Scout units extend their outing season to all 12 months of the year; and to share their acquired knowledge and skills with their units. These skills are taught over six sessions using the patrol method.
What Okpik sessions cover:
Cold Weather Clothing Systems and Sleeping Systems; Cooking, Meal Preparation and Planning; Equipment & Sleds; First Aid and Hypothermia; Travel Safety; Winter Naturalist; Winter Photography; Stoves, Fire building, Leave No Trace; Tents & Shelters. The overnight session introduces participants to a variety of winter activities and games and an opportunity to try out what they learned in a safe environment. Learning is done using the Patrol Method. Okpik also teaches you how to have fun in the cold! Think Klondike Derby for adults and senior Scouts!
Who
: Okpik training is open to all levels of Scout leaders and experienced Scouting youth (Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouts) who are
13 years old
by the date of the Indoor Session. Scouts BSA youth must be 1st class or above.
For scouts that are 13 years old they must have Scoutmaster approval to attend
.
All participants must submit a completed Annual Health & Medical form at the Indoor Session (parts A & B). In addition, all youth participants must submit a completed Activity Consent form at the Indoor Session. Participants must attend all sessions and patrol meetings to complete the course and earn the coveted Okpik cubes
All previous Okpik Participants are invited to join our Staff
to refresh your skills and train the next bunch of eager Okpikians.  Please let us know you'll join us by registering and filling out the google form.

/127-116539.desc:
NATIONAL YOUTH LEADERSHIP TRAINING
WHO:
The Current/Future leaders in your home unit
WHAT:
National Youth Leadership Training
WHEN:
June 13-19 2027
WHERE:
Camp Big Timber
WHY:
Enhance your leadership skills through team building, conflict resolution, communication, and goal setting! All while having fun!
OUT OF COUNCIL TROOPS WELCOME!
Participant Orientation:
Will be held the week prior to the Course
Why NLYT?
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is designed to have youth staff teach leadership skills to youth participants. From beginning to end, it is a YOUTH LEADERSHIP PROGRAM!
NYLT is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops, crews, ships and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a week-long course. Content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ leadership skills much faster.
NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and audio visual support, NYLT participants will be engaged in a unified approach to leadership that will give them the skill and confidence to lead well. Through a wide range of activities, games, and adventures, participants will work and play together as they put into action the best Scouting has to offer.
Participant Requirements
To attend an NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of tthe course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit
Must have a current BSA Annual Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C
Scouts must be at least 13 years of age and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program registration. They must be ranked a First Class Scout or higher and have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 13 years of age and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships and have some basic camping experience
While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant has basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
A unit leader recommendation

/127-MESH27.desc:
Mental, Emotional, and Social Health (MESH) training is a proactive initiative by Scouting America designed to equip staff and adult leaders with the tools to support the holistic well-being of Scouts. Recognizing that the rigors of scouting can create unique stressors, the MESH curriculum focuses on identifying behavioral changes that may indicate a Scout is struggling. By integrating these practices into leader development, councils aim to move beyond physical safety alone, fostering an environment where mental and emotional needs are prioritized with the same urgency as a physical injury.
The training utilizes the U-S-A Model—Understand the behaviors, Speak and Support, and Act and Advocate—to provide a clear, actionable framework for intervention. Participants are trained to recognize signs of mental health challenges and more serious crises, while also learning how to create mentally healthy environments including essential self-care techniques. Ultimately, MESH training serves to reduce the stigma surrounding mental health in Scouting, ensuring that every participant has access to a supportive, empathetic community that is "Prepared" for the complexities of modern youth development.

/127-Okpik2627.desc:
Okpik 2026 - 2027
Cold Weather Outdoor Training
Okpik (Ook’pick) is the Inuit name for a Snowy Owl. The Okpik course aims to provide participants with the skills and knowledge to enjoy an outdoor experience in cold weather; to help Scout units extend their outing season to all 12 months of the year; and to share their acquired knowledge and skills with their units. These skills are taught over six sessions using the patrol method.
What Okpik sessions cover:
Cold Weather Clothing Systems and Sleeping Systems; Cooking, Meal Preparation and Planning; Equipment & Sleds; First Aid and Hypothermia; Travel Safety; Winter Naturalist; Winter Photography; Stoves, Fire building, Leave No Trace; Tents & Shelters. The overnight session introduces participants to a variety of winter activities and games and an opportunity to try out what they learned in a safe environment. Learning is done using the Patrol Method. Okpik also teaches you how to have fun in the cold! Think Klondike Derby for adults and senior Scouts!
Who
: Okpik training is open to all levels of Scout leaders and experienced Scouting youth (Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouts) who are
13 years old
by the date of the Indoor Session. Scouts BSA youth must be 1st class or above.
For scouts that are 13 years old they must have Scoutmaster approval to attend
.
All participants must submit a completed Annual Health & Medical form at the Indoor Session (parts A & B). In addition, all youth participants must submit a completed Activity Consent form at the Indoor Session. Participants must attend all sessions and patrol meetings to complete the course and earn the coveted Okpik cubes
All previous Okpik Participants are invited to join our Staff
to refresh your skills and train the next bunch of eager Okpikians.

/127-WFA2026.desc:
Wilderness First Aid Certification Classes
Emergency Care in Remote Locations, this course provides information on how to handle common injuries and illnesses when medical care is an hour away or more. This class will teach you what to look for and what to do in the event of an emergency, and direct you to the most appropriate type of care.
This class includes
Expanded information on heat and cold emergencies
Updated guidelines for managing snake bite emergencies
New information on managing diabetic emergencies
Skill sheets providing step-by-step visual reviews of procedures discussed
Flow charts reinforcing the decision-making process and appropriate procedures
Decision tables provide a concise summary of what signs first aiders should look for and what treatment steps they should take
All participants in The Wilderness First Aid class should be at least 16 years old. The course is taught at an adult pace and some portions involve treatment and decisions that can be emotionally and physically distressing. The Course Director is authorized to make exceptions. Please contact the Course Director directly prior to registering any youth under 16.
Be prepared to spend some time outdoors during this course. Practice sessions are hands-on.
Lunch will be provided. Please contact the Course Director with any dietary needs.
Attendees must attend both Saturday and Sunday classes to complete training.  This not an overnight event. Classes will start and end each day and participants must be present and on time for both sessions.
A current CPR/AED certification is required for the Wilderness First Aid Certification.  CPR/AED is not taught during this class.  If you do not have a current CPR/AED certification you can sign up for a class at the links below.

Supplement your troop, pack, or crew's planned activities at Camp Sol R. Crown with our NEIC Local Adventures opportunities!
The Northeast Illinois Council welcomes all Cub Scout packs/dens, Scouts BSA troops, and Venturing crews to Camp Sol R. Crown for an open outdoor program.
ACTIVITIES:
You can visit for the day, or your unit can reserve a campsite and stay the weekend.
Archery
Air Rifle/BB Gun
Portable Climbing Wall
BMX Pump Track (subject to volunteer availability). For older Scouts and Adults.

COST
Out-of-council Youth pay an additional $10 per participant.
$15
– Scouts
$15

Free
– Adults

/129-BALOO2027.desc:
Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO) training is a day of fun and learning that will help pack leaders plan and carry out a quality "entry-level" outdoor experience for the Cub Scouts and their families. Participants will better understand the laws of the BSA and camp programming while acquiring the skills and confidence to host a successful campout by increasing their knowledge of available resources and using national and local council standards as guidelines.
Location:
Camp Sol R. Crown
Dates:
May 1 and 2, 2027
Pricing:
$20 in-council | $30 out-of-council
Safeguarding Youth Training (SYT):
Adults, please provide your SYT completion date and ensure your training is current (not expired) throughout the time of the event.
BALOO Training Covers:
Preparations for camping with Cub Scouts
Site selection
Parental involvement
Health and safety
Equipment
Feeding
Introduction to outdoor skills
REQUIRED FOR CUB SCOUT CAMPING:
The BALOO course is required for all packs that want to go camping. At least one adult (leader or parent) camping with the pack must be “BALOO certified.” This course is only offered 1-2 times annually,
so sign up today!
FEES FOR NEIC ADULTS:
Upon successful completion of the BALOO course, fees for Northeast Illinois Council members will be refunded.

/129-FirstAidMeet2027.desc:
The First Aid Meet is an opportunity for teams to demonstrate first aid expertise in a competitive situation. In each of four problems, Scouts are presented with emergency situations. Each team will be judged on its assessment of the victims, determination of appropriate treatments, and cooperation to provide effective care. The event provides Scouts with a chance to diagnose a problem, strengthen known first-aid skills, learn new techniques, and demonstrate leadership and teamwork.
Please see the attached First Aid Meet guidebook for the prerequisites for each team and information about preparing for the meet.
Safeguarding Youth Training required:
All adult participants are required to provide their SYT completion date and be current (not expired) at the time of the event.
This event is open to all troops and crews in NEIC.
There is a limit of 15 teams.
A team is composed of 6–9 Scouts, and troops are encouraged to have more than one team
Note: The minimum size team of 6 allows two members to act as victims
Each team must provide an adult who will serve as a problem judge

/129-IndoorRifleDec2027.desc:
Join us for our March indoor rifle merit badge day!
Get ready for a fun, hands-on day of rifle shooting! Trained and qualified volunteers will guide Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crews through the Rifle Shooting Merit Badge. Scouts can complete the badge in its entirety or focus just on the shooting portion—bring your blue card and join the fun!indoor rifle merit badge day!
Cost – one session: 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. (possibly 2 p.m.)
$10
–
NEIC Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crew members
$20
– Out-of-council Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crew members
When
: Sunday, December 12, 2027
Pre-course preparation
Print and complete requirements 1 and 2, Section B from the workbook and bring your filled copy to check in.
These are on pages 1–3 and 8–10:
http://usscouts.org/mb/worksheets/rifle-shooting.pdf
Using Scoutbook (recommended)? Assign Matt Maj (mmaj1999@yahoo.com) as your rifle merit badge counselor ahead of time if possible.
Using blue cards? Bring your own. Scoutbook makes tracking easier, but either option works.
Requirements
Read the Rifle Shooting Merit Badge (MB) pamphlet
Review the requirements: Option B for air rifles
Print, complete, and bring the worksheet (Option B for air rifles)
Bring a completed blue card signed by troop Scoutmaster
Class Structure
We’ll start the day with a safety briefing—please arrive on time so we can get started together.
Scouts will be split into two groups: one group will do bookwork while the other practices shooting and cleaning. Groups will rotate to complete all requirements.
Participants can finish their merit badge requirements before the 1:30 p.m. end time; if finished early, the extra time can be used for more shooting fun!
Participant limits
We have five lanes, with five shooters at a time, rotating with others.
If fewer than 20 sign up, each Scout will get more time on the range.

Get ready for a fun, hands-on day of rifle shooting! Trained and qualified volunteers will guide Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crews through the Rifle Shooting Merit Badge. Scouts can complete the badge in its entirety or focus just on the shooting portion—bring your blue card and join the fun!
Cost – one session: 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. (possibly 2 p.m.)
$15
–
NEIC Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crew members
$25
– Out-of-council Scouts BSA youth and Venturing crew members
When
: Sunday, March 7, 2027
Pre-course preparation
Print and complete requirements 1 and 2, Section B from the workbook and bring your filled copy to check in.
Rifle Merit Badge Worksheet
.
Using Scoutbook (recommended)? Assign Matt Maj (mmaj1999@yahoo.com) as your rifle merit badge counselor ahead of time if possible.
Using blue cards? Bring your own. Scoutbook makes tracking easier, but either option works.
Requirements
Read the Rifle Shooting Merit Badge (MB) pamphlet
Review the requirements: Option B for air rifles
Print, complete, and bring the worksheet (Option B for air rifles)
Bring a completed blue card signed by troop Scoutmaster
Class structure
We’ll start the day with a safety briefing—please arrive on time so we can get started together.
Scouts will be split into two groups: one group will do bookwork while the other practices shooting and cleaning. Groups will rotate to complete all requirements.
Participants can finish their merit badge requirements before the 1:30 p.m. end time; if finished early, the extra time can be used for more shooting fun!
Participant limits
We have five lanes, with five shooters at a time, rotating with others.
If fewer than 20 sign up, each Scout will get more time on the range.
CLICK HERE
if your troop or crew also wants to do cold-weather tent camping one of these weekends. This link takes you directly to the Camp Crown reservation page. IMPORTANT: Reservations by families are not permitted. They can only be completed by BSA units.

/129-KlondikeDerby2027.desc:
The Klondike Derby is a day of fun and friendly competition in the snow (or mud, or sun—you never know with Midwest winters). Troops compete against each other in activities like fire building, sled racing, and first aid, carrying all their supplies on a troop-designed sled.
This is one of our most popular Scouts BSA and Venturing crew activities. Arrow of Light Scouts may attend as guests of a troop.
Safeguarding Youth Training required:
All adult participants must provide their SYT completion date and be current (not expired) at the time of the event.
Eligibility:
Limited to Scouts BSA troops and Venturing crews. Arrow of Light Scouts may attend as guests.
PATROL SIZE IS A MINIMUM OF FIVE AND MAXIMUM OF NINE,
with at least two adults for each troop or crew registration. Arrow of Light guests can participate as a sled crew member and be counted towards the maximum of nine patrol members, but for hesitant Arrow of Light Scouts that would rather tag along and observe, sign them up, but don't count them as part of the sled crew numbers. (Parents with up-to-date SYT are welcome to attend as accompanying adults and should work with their unit leader to register.) If there are 10 or more Scouts, form multiple patrols.
Lunch:
There is an additional $10 fee for Saturday Lunch.
Camping
:
Troops can camp Friday and/or Saturday night and should work with the Klondike Event Chair, Michael Cunningham (
scoutmastertroop52deerfield@gmail.com
) to reserve a campsite.

/129-MSRFamilyAdvCamp2027.desc:
Attention all Cub Scout packs and families!
Join us at our overnight camp nestled in the scenic Northwoods.
Family Adventure Camp (formerly Akela Camp) is held at Ma-Ka-Ja-Wan Scout Reservation in Pearson, Wisconsin. Cub Scouts will experience an immersive Scouting program, from swimming and boating at the waterfront to hiking, leatherworking, target sports, and sleeping in beautiful East Camp. Scouts will have access to the full resources of a world-class Scouting camp.
Your time at camp is certainly one you want to share alongside your fellow den families, but it is not required. Your family is welcome to register for and attend camp, even if your pack is unable to join. Also, families and dens from the same Cub Scout pack will camp together, even if separate registrations are completed. Contact Debi if you have questions about registering online (see Contacts for her email and others). If your den has a den chief, they are welcome to participate!
This four-day, three-night experience allows your Cub Scout to gain a sense of independence and have unplugged off-screen fun, all while earning advancement and learning new skills. Campers can go swimming and boating at the waterfront, hiking around the camp, and work on their Scouting skills at various program areas.
Safeguarding Youth Training Required:
All Adult Participants must provide their SYT Completion Date and must be valid throughout your time at camp (it cannot expire while you are there).
Health Forms -
This Cub Scout Camp is for less than 72 consecutive hours, so only Parts A and B are needed. Go to "Attachments" for the informational page, and the link to the National website to download the most current version.
Where is it?
Ma-Ka-Ja-Wan Scout Reservation, W6500 Spring Lake Road, Pearson, WI
Who can attend?
Wolf Scouts
(Who will be in 2nd grade in the Fall of 2027)
Bear Scouts
(Who will be in 3rd grade in the Fall of 2027)
Webelos
(Who will be in 4th grade in the Fall of 2027)
Arrow of Light Scouts
(Who will be in 5th grade in the Fall of 2027)
Den Chiefs
(
Scouts BSA Youth
who have completed Den Chief Training)
Adult Leaders/Parents
(including
Den
Leaders
)
Siblings!
(Lion Cubs and Tiger Cubs included)
When is it?
To better suit your pack, den, or family's busy summer schedules, we have two available sessions. For each session, arrive 1 to 4 PM to check in, and leave camp by 9:30 AM.
July 4-7, 2027
July 7-10, 2027
What is the cost?
TO BE DETERMINED
What does the camp provide?
Sturdy two-person tents on wooden platforms off the ground:
Each campsite has pre-assembled tents with 2 cots in each tent.
All Meals:
You will eat in our historic East Camp Dining Hall and participate in mealtime activities with our camp staff.
Dedicated Camp Staff:
Our staff is trained to safely provide your Scouting Families with the best camp experience possible.
Wifi
is available to adults for any business or remote work needs during your stay
.
Here is a short list of activities you and your Scouts can enjoy:
Swimming
Stargazing
Nature trails
Boating
Fishing
Hiking
Visiting our own Horse Ranch to pet or ride a horse!
Range & Target Sports
Starring in campfire skits or songs
Camp-wide games
Learning new Scout skills
Crafts you can make and take home
And Much More!
(Adults get to have fun doing many of these activities, too!)
Will I know anyone there?
You will if you bring your friends! Unless otherwise requested, we will assign you to the same campsite as other Scouts from your pack, den, or local area.

/129-NYLT2027.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is an immersive and wide-ranging six-day outdoor experience for Scouting America youth programs.
The course will be conducted at the Ma-Ka-Ja-Wan Scout Reservation by a trained staff of youth and adult leaders from around the Northeast Illinois Council. The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, KNOW, and DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW to apply what is learned. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a quest for the meaning of leadership.
COURSE LIMIT:
The NYLT course is limited to the first 54 Participants to register, so sign up today!
REQUIRED HEALTH FORM:
The Annual Health Form (Parts A, B, and C) is due by April 17. Contact Patty with questions.
PARENTS:
Scouts must be at least 13 years old on the first day of the course to participate.
Contact their Unit Leader if they are interested because only Scouts approved by their adult leaders may attend.
UNIT LEADERS:
Contact Debi Geiger or Tony Giamis for the passcode to register Scouts.
STAFF:
Approved Staff will be given their registration password after their interview.
REGISTRATION CLOSES:
May 20, 2027 (11:59 PM).
All Fees must be paid in full by then.
$340
– Scout Early Discount Fee if registered and paid in full by April 30, 2027 (11:59 PM)
$380
*
– Scout Regular Fee begins May 1.
$80
– New Youth or Adult Staff
No Fee
– Returning Youth or Adult Staff
*
The system will automatically increase a Scout's fee from $340 to $380 on May 1 if they have a balance due. Contact Debi with questions.
Items Included in Fee:
Participants will be contacted to provide sizes for each item included with the fee.
TRANSPORTATION:
The NYLT program includes transportation via Coach Bus Service to and from the Ma-Ka-Ja-Wan Scout Reservation.  Details regarding the time and location are available in the ATTACHMENTS as well as the bus waiver if the Scout will be picked up directly at the end of the program.
ORIENTATION:
A mandatory "Parent & Participant" orientation is scheduled for April 17 at Camp Crown. This orientation will begin at 9 am - a reminder will be sent to all registered Scouts and parents. At this event, we will verify all medical and diet concerns, present the "week-in-a-glance" view for all parents and guardians, refresh the Scout Skills needed through the "Orientation Trail" with the participants and youth staff (8 stations), and answer all questions. Scoutmasters are invited to attend.

/138-2027WoodBadge.desc:
Wood Badge
A two-weekend immersion and practice of advance leadership training for Scouters.
* Both weekend sessions are required to complete the course
.
First Weekend: April 23 - 25, 2027.
Second Weekend: May 15 - 16, 2027.
$300 / $320 after March 8, 2027
Ingersoll Scout Reservation
What is Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is the advanced leadership training in the Scouting America Training Continuum. It is for registered adults in all areas of Scouting: Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Commissioners, District volunteers, and Council members. The only requirements are basic training for your registered position and the desire to learn and have fun.
The course is designed to help you become the best leader you can be — at home, at church, in your community, at work, and, of course, in Scouting. You will gain skills you can use your entire life. We expect the best from our Scouts and they have the right to expect the same from us. Your Scouts need your help now to become the leaders of tomorrow. Wood Badge is a great way to ensure that you are ready to show them the way.
Why Take Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is designed primarily to further the training of adult leaders in Scouting America.  By continuing the training of these adult leaders, Wood Badge enhances the overall program offered to the youth members in Scouting America and facilitates our goals of youth leadership development.  Participants learn techniques that make them better leaders, and they learn how to lead groups to achieve objectives.
Who Should Attend?
Wood Badge is high-powered leadership training for adult leaders in all Scouting America programs – Cub Scouting,  Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouting – as well as Council and District leaders.  This includes all assistants and committee members.
There are no minimum tenure requirements.  In fact, leaders are encouraged to attend Wood Badge as early in their Scouting careers as they can, preferably within two years of becoming involved.  But long-time Scouters will benefit equally.
Participants must have completed the basic training requirements for their Scouting position. Click here to get additional information on what the basic requirements are.
Spots are very limited. Only 48 of the W. D. Boyce Council’s  hundreds of Scout leaders can be accommodated in each class.

/160-VoyageurSpring27.desc:
VOYAGEUR
Canoe Training & Paddle Craft Safety
Youth and Adult Training
The Voyageur Canoe Training Program was established in the Central Indiana Council (now Crossroads of America Council) of the Boy Scouts of America following the death of two scouts during a canoe trip to Quetico Provincial Park in 1964. In response to this tragedy, the Voyageur Canoe Training program was established to provide adult leaders and youth with the canoe skills and trip planning skills necessary to avoid accidents like this from ever occurring again. The training is open to any adult over 18 registered with the BSA, as well as to youth over 14 who are registered with the BSA.
Objective:  To prepare youth and adults to take the Voyageur program back to their unit and conduct safe canoe outings including High Adventure trips. To hold the older Scouts' interest and keep them active in the Scouting program. To encourage younger Scouts to earn rank advancement. To provide canoeing adventure for Venture Crews.
How can Adults obtain or renew their BSA Canoe Paddle Craft Safety Certification?
Adults that complete prerequisites (Safe Swim Defense and Safety Afloat), attend the entire course, and pass the written test will obtain their BSA Paddle Craft Safety - Canoe certification. All certification requirements (except the swimmer test, Safe Swim Defense, and Safety Afloat) are taught during the course, and certification testing is conducted. Kayaking certification is available for an additional charge and requires an additional day of coursework.
Adult leaders may renew their Paddle Craft Safety certification by attending the one-day Paddle Craft Safety recertification day on the second Saturday of the course. Participants will be tested and need to pass the performance and written requirements to obtain recertification.
Additional information and prerequisites
Participants should be aware that spouses, significant others, friends, and unit mates will not be assigned to the same canoe.  This policy has been developed through years of ‘what could possibly go wrong’ experiences.  Tandem canoeing can be challenging to learn without the additional stress of relationship dynamics, and we wish all our participants to leave the course with the same friends and family members that they began the course with.
Please bring the following completed required documentation with you to the first day of course:
Bring your BSA Registration number with you.
Current Scout Health Form-Minimum Sections A & B Scout health form.
Current documentation of “swimmer” classification
from camp or from your unit swim check.  Must be current/within the last year.
This is required for participation.
Additional requirements for adults:
Proof of current Youth Protection Training.
Proof of current Safe Swim Defense and Safety Afloat certifications.
Please see the attached forms and welcome information.

The Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills (IOLS) expands the concepts of Scoutmaster training and provides Scouters with the confidence to take youth into the outdoors. The course emphasizes the patrol method of Scout-led troop programs. Participants should complete the course with confidence to take Scouts safely into the outdoors. Along with Scoutmaster Specifics, this course is required of all direct contact leaders registered in Scout Troops to be considered “trained”.
BALOO is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities. BALOO training consists of an online pre-requisite component in addition to an overnight hands-on practical. Scouting America's Cub Scout level camping policies will be taught along with the discovery of the necessary tools to help units carry our a successful camping experience. Completion of this course is mandatory for a MINIMUM OF ONE adult on a Pack overnighter.
These courses are an excellent foundation for the more advanced Wood Badge course.

/165-114652.desc:
*Please note that NYLT will opperate under Central Timezone as its location will be at Camp Topenebee*
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others. The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what they must KNOW, and what they must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
NYLT is a six-day course. Content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on the immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ leadership skills much faster.
In order to attend an NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members  must be at least 13. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops*
Venturers and Sea Scouts (male and female) must be at least 13 or 14, have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They should have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships*. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.
*ILST, ILSC, and ILSS can be completed within the unit and will also be offered at
Camp Tamarack Summer Camp

Whether you're looking for a fun-filled day, an overnight getaway, or a multi-night adventure, we have the perfect Cub Scout camp experience for you. STEM Harvest: Cub Scout Rocket & Space Exploration Program
Space is like a giant playground in the sky—filled with stars to discover, planets to explore, robots to control, and mysteries waiting to be solved!
As part of STEM Harvest, Cub Scouts will take part in a full day of hands-on science, technology, engineering, and exploration.
Join Steve Arthur, NASA/JPL Solar System Ambassador and Founder of Big Creek Rocketry, to learn about the history of rockets and spaceflight, discover how rockets work, and build your own rocket.
Scouts will also experience astronomy through the Fort Hays State University inflatable astronomy dome, explore stars, planets, and constellations, and take part in a robotics station focused on engineering, technology, and space exploration.
Lunch will be on your own. After lunch, families will reconvene at the designated launch site at 1:00 PM for the grand finale: the rocket launch!
Scouts will get to launch the rockets they built and see STEM concepts come to life.
Rocket launch is weather permitting.
Build. Explore. Discover. Launch. STEM Harvest!

Wednesday, November 11, at 11:59 p.m.
Who Can Attend?
Arrow of Light Scouts, Scouts BSA youth, Venturing youth, Sea Scouts, and registered adult leaders are invited to participate. Arrow of Light dens or patrols must attend with two-deep leadership from their den, patrol, or pack. All adults attending must be registered in a Scouting America program and current in Safeguarding Youth Training.

Participant
Fee through November 1 at 11:59 p.m.
Arrow of Light, Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scout youth
$25 per person
Adults
$15 per person

Saturday Cooking Activities & Patrol Competition
Saturday features stations covering a variety of cooking topics, followed by a
patrol competition from 2:30–3:30 p.m.
Units will then have time to cook and prepare their contributions to the evening meal. The final station schedule and location map will be provided at Friday evening's leadership meeting.
Saturday's Scoutgiving Fellowship Dinner
Come together for a Thanksgiving-style dinner with Scouts and leaders from across the district.
Meat will be provided.
Each unit must prepare at least one side dish or dessert in camp to share.
Side dishes should serve 40–50 people.
Please label your serving vessel.
5:00 p.m.:
One Scout from each troop reports to the Dining Center to assist with final meal preparations (KP duty).
5:45 p.m.:
Units deliver their dishes to the Dining Center.
6:00 p.m.:
Closing flags.
6:10–7:30 p.m.:
Scoutgiving dinner.
Adult volunteers are requested to help with meal preparation, serving, and cleanup. Everyone must bring their own plates, cups, and utensils and wash them at their campsite afterward. Units are responsible for all other meals.
What Units Need to Prepare
Charcoal:
Bring one 10-pound bag per unit and turn it in at Friday evening's leadership meeting.
Cooking supplies:
Bring the food and equipment needed for unit meals and your shared dish, plus your own firewood for the weekend.
Health forms:
Bring completed Parts A and B for every attendee. Forms must be turned in to the camp medical officer at check-in and collected at checkout.
Food allergies:
Notify event leadership before the event about any Scout or leader food allergies.
Friday leadership meeting:
The Senior Patrol Leader, Chaplain's Aide, and one Scoutmaster must attend the 9:30 p.m. meeting and cracker barrel in the Dining Center.

9:00 a.m.

9:30–11:30 a.m.
Units leaving Saturday may check out from
7:30–8:30 p.m.
All units must check out with Camporee staff in the Dining Center before departing. Medical forms will be returned and patches provided after the campsite is inspected and cleared.

/192-Konzavous2027.desc:
Konzavous: Frontier Adventure 2027
More than a camporee. A destination experience.
Join Scouts, leaders, and families from across Kansas and the surrounding region for
Konzavous: Frontier Adventure 2027
, a one-of-a-kind immersive frontier experience hosted by the Republican Valley Muzzleloaders Association (RVMA) and the Konza District.
Located on the historic RVMA grounds west of Wakefield, Kansas, Konzavous transforms a typical Scout campout into a living frontier village where participants step back in time and experience the skills, challenges, and adventure of America's mountain men and early pioneers.
Inspired by the great rendezvous gatherings of the fur trade era, Konzavous is designed to be a destination event that Scouts look forward to all year. Throughout the weekend, participants won't simply watch demonstrations—they will actively learn, practice, and experience authentic frontier skills from knowledgeable historians, craftsmen, and outdoorsmen.
Experience the Frontier
Scouts may have opportunities to:
• Throw tomahawks and learn their historical uses
• Shoot black powder rifles under trained supervision
• Master flint and steel fire starting
• Build fires using primitive friction methods
• Explore leatherworking and frontier craftsmanship
• Learn traditional bow-making techniques
• Practice archery skills
• Discover trapping methods used by early frontiersmen
• Explore hide tanning and wilderness survival skills
• Visit authentic camps and interact with living-history interpreters
Why Attend?
Konzavous is not just another camporee. It is an opportunity for Scouts to immerse themselves in a hands-on outdoor experience unlike any other offered in the region. The combination of authentic frontier skills, living history, outdoor adventure, and fellowship creates memories that last a lifetime.
Whether you are a first-year Scout or an experienced outdoorsman, you'll discover new skills, meet fellow adventurers, and experience a weekend that feels like stepping into another era.
Important Notes
• There will NOT be a trading area at this event. Please do not bring trade goods or items intended for barter.
• Personal firearms, black powder equipment, archery equipment, and tomahawks are NOT permitted. All program equipment will be provided and supervised by event staff.
• A map of program areas and activity locations will be distributed during the Friday evening leaders' meeting.
A Kansas Scout Tradition in the Making
Our vision is simple: to make Konzavous the premier frontier-themed Scout event in the Midwest—a place where Scouts travel from across Kansas and neighboring states to experience adventure, history, and the spirit of the American frontier.
Gather your patrol. Pack your gear. Step back in time.
The frontier awaits at Konzavous: Frontier Adventure 2027

What is ScoutCon?
It’s a weekend of being electronically unplugged enjoying fellowship with others playing board games, competing in tournaments, costume contest and other fun activities.
Enjoy our library of over 100 different board games
. Everyone is welcome to bring some of their own games to put into the library for everyone’s enjoyment.
ScoutCon is primarily indoor activities and will happen in rain, shine, or snow. Please bring your own tent and be prepared for cold weather camping!
ScoutCon! is open to registered Scouts BSA, Sea Scouts, Venturers, and Adult Leaders. Must be current on your registration and YPT to participate.
COSPLAY COSTUME CONTEST
: No actual fire-arms allowed for this event. Weapons for cosplay must be clearly manufactured costume props and rated PG-13, represent a game/story lore.
TOURNAMENTS
: Everyone must demonstrate excellent sportsmanship, befitting a Scout, and win or lose gracefully.
GAMES, GAMES, GAMES
: From popular roleplaying games like Dungeons & Dragons ™, Dungeon Crawl Classics ™ (“DCC”), Shadowrun ™, and Star Wars RPG ™ to boardgames such as Settlers of Catan ™, Ticket to Ride ™, RISK ™, and Monopoly ™ to Magic the Gathering ™, UNO ™, and simple card games…ScoutCon! is where the fun happens, year after year!

The induction process will challenge you, inspire you, and help you grow as a leader in the Scouting community.
Here’s what you can expect:
Induction Ceremony: Experience the powerful and memorable ceremonial process that marks your official entry into the OA.
Service Projects: Participate in meaningful service to improve your local Scout properties and give back to the community.
Leadership Development: Learn from experienced Arrowmen about how you can contribute to your unit and the OA chapter in new and impactful ways.
Brotherhood and Fellowship: Connect with fellow Scouts who share your commitment to the principles of the OA and enjoy a weekend of fun, adventure, and camaraderie.
The weekend will also include plenty of time for fellowship with new and returning Arrowmen, as well as opportunities to get to know the rich history and traditions of the OA. Whether you're completing your Induction Experience or preparing for Brotherhood, this event is the perfect way to take the next step in your Scouting adventure.
If your Unit has had their election and you were elected, join us at the next Induction Experience by registering below.
Onsite check-in will be between 6:00 and 7:00 pm, on Friday of the event at the Administration Building (by the red gate). Please arrive as early as possible. If you cannot arrive before 8:00 pm please call Chris Baker by Thursday @ 225-572-4372 or e-mail Chris Baker. We will attempt to accommodate late arrivals. Arrive in your work clothes for Saturday, no need to be in your field uniform. Friday dinner/supper will not be served, so eat before arrival or bring your food. You are expected to stay for the Sunday activities, including the General Lodge meeting. Sunday activities will conclude by 10:00 am.
Fees:
Order of the Arrow New Member (has not completed their Induction) $60 (includes OA dues)
Order of the Arrow Member going through the Induction Experience $20 (additional $30 if you have not paid OA dues)
Order of the Arrow Members $30 (additional $30 if you have not paid OA dues)

/211-WinterCampAvondale.desc:
Welcome to 2026 Winter Camp
We are excited about your Troop attending our 2026 Winter Camp at
Camp Avondale
on the Avondale Scout Reservation!
Winter Camp is a five (5) full-day camp of merit badge classes before the Thanksgiving holiday starting on November 20 (Friday), with classes starting at 9:00 a.m. on November 21  and ends at 12:00 p.m. on November 25. This allows units to camp together using the Troop and Patrol method to accomplish their goals under their own leadership. An excellent Camp Staff provides program help, guidance, and supervision in the areas of Scout Craft, Nature, Shooting Sports, and STEM, along with many other specialty merit badge subjects.
The 2026 Winter Camp Schedule:
Date: November 20-25, 2026
Check-In on Friday, November 20, 2026 from 3:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.
Check-In on Saturday: 7:45 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., November 21, 2026 - Classes begin at 9:00 a.m.
Departure Time: No later than 10:00 a.m., November 25, 2026
Reservation & Fees:
Winter Camp is limited to the
first 200 Scouts.
The cost is $225.00 per Scout for the Discount (Early) Fee until September 15, 2026. Beginning September 16, 2026, the On-Time Fee is $250.00 until October 31, 2026.  Beginning November 1, 2026, the Late Fee is $275.00 until registration closes at the end of the day on November 15, 2026. Merit Badges cannot be selected until full payment is made. Some classes have additional fees and these extra class costs are added when the course is selected. Payments via credit card or check will be charged a 3% convenience fee.
If the Scout would like to purchase a T-shirt (short or long-sleeve) or a hooded shirt (regular or lightweight), please make sure to
place the order by November 1, 2026
, and select the appropriate item under the 'Product' field at checkout.
All adults attending camp must register as an adult leader or as staff (application on-line).
The adult fee is $85.00 per adult
($100.00 starting September 16, 2026; $120 starting November 1, 2026)
.
Additionally, an adult Scouting America application must be completed if the adult is not currently registered with Scouting America.
Staff will not pay a fee. If Staff would like to purchase a T-shirt (short or long-sleeve) or a hooded shirt (regular or lightweight), please make sure to
place the order by November 1, 2026
, and select the appropriate item under the 'Product' field at checkout.  Staff registration must be completed by end of day on October 1, 2026.
Adult Leaders:
Two registered adult leaders, 21 years of age or over, are required with current Safeguarding Youth Training in camp at all times.
All adults accompanying a Scouting unit must be registered as leaders or committee members.
Female Scouts BSA must be accompanied by a registered Female Leader.
Sign Up as MBC or Camp Staff
Merit Badge Counselors (MBCs) and Staff resources must be approved ahead of registration.
Staff Application
Health Forms:
All Scouts and Adults attending camp must have a current Annual Health and Medical Record Parts A, B, and C. This is necessary to document the current health status and medications, if any, that the Scout or Adult is taking. Health forms will be returned to units at the end of camp. It is recommended that only copies of the health forms be submitted. (The originals should remain with Troop records.)

/211-YSC_27.desc:
The South Louisiana Council’s annual Youth Sporting Clays Classic will be held on Saturday, April 10, 2027.
The Avondale Scout Reservation will host the event again this year, but we have a new course location. Perkins Lodge is this year’s choice of location, which means an all-new course design. This event is open to all registered Scouts, BSA, Venturers, and Explorers. The course will consist of multiple sporting clay shooting stations set throughout the Camp Tigator/Perkins Lodge area. NRA-certified shotgun instructors will travel with the shooting groups to every station.
Shotguns, ammunition, targets, awards, and campsites are all included for all registered participants. The registration deadline is April 2, 2027, 11:59 p.m. You can come up for the day or camp for the weekend. Campsite fees will be waived for pre-registered participants for the weekend.
Registration for youth participants is $45.00 per person if registered by April 2, 2027. Registrations received between April 3, 2027, and April 10, 2027, will be assessed a $10.00 late fee per participant.
Spectators who are not shooters are invited to come and support their favorite team. Spectator admission is $20.00 for the day and includes breakfast and lunch.
Accompanying adult Scouters and parents will have the opportunity to walk the course with your Scouts and shoot the course. Adults who wish to shoot the course are subject to the same event rules and regulations as Scouts. The “Adult Walk” registration is $45.00 per person if registered no later than April 2, 2027. Adult registrations received between April 3, 2027, and April 10, 2027, will be assessed a $10.00 late fee per adult registration.  This covers shotguns, ammunition, targets, food, and awards.
NO PERSONAL FIREARMS allowed for this event!
Overview of the day’s events:
All participants should park in the Perkins Lodge parking lot and go to the lodge for registration/check-in, coffee, and a light breakfast. After check-in, all participants will attend a mandatory safety briefing. After the mandatory safety briefing, the assigned groups, accompanied by their NRA-certified shotgun instructors, will be directed to their designated starting points on the course. We will be utilizing a shotgun start for the event.
Once all groups have completed their round, we will gather at the Dining Hall for a jambalaya lunch, provided by a group of shooting sports enthusiast volunteers. We will present awards and door prizes after lunch. After the awards ceremony, youth shooters who want a little more time behind a shotgun are welcome to hang out with our NRA RSOs and Instructors at their favorite station. We will shoot until the sun goes down or the supplies run out, whichever comes first.
Looking for volunteers:
If you are a certified NRA Shotgun Instructor or NRA RSO and would like to help with the event, please contact us.
We are also looking for trappers and dedicated scorers. No prior experience is necessary; we have a GREAT on-the-job training program!
We're excited to offer an annual sporting clays event and give our youth a fun, safe, and memorable shooting experience here at the Avondale Scout Reservation. Come check out the fun, support your youth, volunteer your expertise, or all of the above!
We look forward to seeing you on the course.

Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation Training (BALOO)
BALOO is the Cub Scout leader training required for any Cub Scout den or pack campout, including pack camping overnighters and Webelos den overnighters. Packs are required to have at least 1 BALOO trained leader in attendance at every campout.
BALOO training is comprised of
two
components—
an online component
and a practical, hands-on component. Both components must be completed to qualify as a “TRAINED” Cub Scout outdoor leader.
The online component (available on my.scouting.org) must be completed prior to the practical component, in order to make the best use of time to allow leaders to experience as much as possible during the practical hands-on training.
Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS)
IOLS is the Outdoor training component required to be trained as a Scoutmaster/Assistant Scoutmaster.  The course will lead the participant through the Be, Know and Do’s of how to deliver instruction in a youth-led BSA unit.  We will cover the Basic Scout Skills in Tenderfoot, Second Class, First Class from the point of view of teaching youth to lead and teach other youth.  It’s a fun course! We’ll camp, cook, and learn together.
You’ll learn: How to deliver outdoor skills instruction in a youth-led program, covering basic scout skills while camping, cooking, having fun.
When:
Training begins at 8:00am on Saturday, Sept 14 and concludes at 12:00 PM on Sunday, Sept. 15.
Cost:
$20 (to cover food expense)     **Pre-registration is required for meal planning purposes.
Meals:
Participants should plan to eat breakfast prior to arriving.
Lunch and Dinner will be provided on Saturday, and Breakfast will be provided on Sunday.
Required paperwork:
Health Form Parts A-B,
Dietary Restrictions
must be communicated through email .

Be Prepared to “sleep in a tent you helped pitch," Tent, sleeping bag, etc.
If you need electricity to power or charge your breathing machines, please let us know ahead of time so we can accommodate.
Scouts BSA or Cub Scout Handbook, pen/pencils and notepad

Kennebec Valley District Lego Derby
Join us on November 7, 2026 from 9-4 at Camp Bomazeen to create your own Legos Derby ride. Open to all unit levels and families. Bring a friend!
Fill out either the Google
registration form
to hold your place. On race day you will build your vehicle Legos creation then race it all in one day. Come with some creative ideas. Bring your own Legos, if you want. We have plenty to search through.
Pay in person $20.00/person. First 50 kits pre-ordered. Please contact Julie McKenney
julie.m.scouts@gmail.com
by Nov. 3rd to lock in your kit if you can’t fill out the registration form. These are shipped from FL and we place the order at the end of October.
If you return with your base kit from last year, there will be a $5.00 discount.
What is included in your Kit? Nib Base (.45oz), 3.6oz axles, and Legos.
LEGO DERBY RULES
Weight limit - 9oz
Nothing shall be placed any further ahead than the front edge of either the front tires or nib plate. The car may be as long on the back as you wish.
No accelerants or CO2. Gravity led only!
Axles may be placed anywhere under the nib plate. Clamp them down with pliers to force a good hold or carefully glue in place.
The vehicle may not exceed 2 ¾” wide or past the outermost edge of the tires.
Total height may not exceed 5 inches, including any figures or decorations.
Participants are encouraged to super glue any pieces that they feel may come loose in the race. Adjustments will be determined by judges.
HAVE FUN! SCHEDULE
9-10 - Registration - Pick up materials.
9-11 - Build time!
11:00 - Weigh-in & Inspection. No alterations!
Lunch- Derby Diner Host - enjoy the concession sale.
12:00 - Race time! May start sooner if ready
3:00- Awards to follow race.
Clean up - Many hands make light work
Final Note:
Due to the time of year in Maine, the camp will be winterized and heat source limited. Please feel free to dress in layers, wear winter hats, bring camp chairs and personal water bottles. We have latrines for use in Hillside.

/220-26conservation.desc:
Conservation Service Projects
3rd Saturday of each Month
Broad Creek Memorial Scout Reservation
1929 Susquehanna Hall Road
Whiteford, MD  21160
9:00 AM - Noon
Are you a Scout or leader of Scouts looking for service hours? Are you and your unit looking to make a difference? Come to Broad Creek Scout Reservation and help maintain some of our most precious outdoor resources.
On the third Saturday of every month, the Council Conservation Committee coordinates a service project benefitting the land conservation at Broad Creek. These projects are designed to meet the 3-hour conservation project requirement for Life Rank, with Unit Leader approval.
Note that youth who are attending must have adult supervision to accompany them, in line with Scouting's Youth Protection guidelines.
Those participating in the projects should meet at the Rosenberg Welcome Center at 9am Saturday morning and plan to be done around noon.

/220-27bcsc.desc:
Nestled between the rolling hills of Harford County and the rolling waves of the Susquehanna River, Broad Creek is at the heart of Scouting adventure. From conquering the climbing tower to kayaking through a forest stream into deeper waters, Scout Camp at Broad Creek is guaranteed to have a new experience in store for each visit. Welcome to Baltimore’s flagship camping experience!
Details on the program will be available at a later date. To view details on summer camp for 2027, check out our webpage at
www.BroadCreekScouting.org/Summer
.
Weeks of Camp
Week 1: June 27 - July 3
Week 2: July 4 - 10
Week 3: July 11 - 17
Week 4: July 18 - 24
Note: To simplify recordkeeping, the unit will maintain a single registration for the unit. Units have access to edit and update their registrations to add, subtract, and change participants, and access advancement records. If you are attending camp with a unit, please register for camp through your unit leadership.
Individuals registering as provisional campers should select "provisional youth" and/or "provisional adult" upon registering.

/220-VSD26Patch.desc:
Valkyrie Service Day Patch
Purchase your 2026 Valkyrie Service Day patch here.
We will have patches ready for pick-up at Shamrock Park, 39 N Hickory Ave, Bel Air, MD 21014, Nov 14 starting at 9:30.
Patches will also be available to ship or held on by the Harford District Executive, Sam Mitchell, to grab someday after the event.
Patches will also be available for purchase on-site during the event. On-site sales will be cash only and will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.
Valkyrie Service Day is a nationwide movement of community service, in loving memory of Bel Air scout Mackenzie Opdyke who passed away after a battle with brain cancer at 10 years old.
Kenzie left our world in a better place because of her curiosity and love and service to others, so we honor her by living our lives in the same manner- let’s leave each place better than we found it, learn to be more curious of the world and how it works, and always remember to help each other.
Mailed patches will be shipped after the event
This year's event is on- November 14, 2026.
