/234-ScoutBSACamp2027.desc:
Adventure. Friendship. Skills. Memories.
Join us for an unforgettable week of Scouts BSA Summer Camp at Camp Moses!
Summer camp gives Scouts the opportunity to experience the best of Scouting while enjoying a full week outdoors with their troop and friends. Whether this is your first summer at Camp Moses or you are returning for another great year, there is something for everyone.
Your Summer Adventure Awaits!
During the week, Scouts will have opportunities to participate in a variety of exciting programs and activities, including:
Merit Badge programs
Swimming and waterfront activities
Shooting sports
Outdoor skills
Nature and conservation programs
Games and recreational activities
Campfires and special camp programs
Leadership and advancement opportunities
Time to build friendships and make lasting memories
Programs and activities may vary based on age, availability, weather, and program schedules.
Troop Camping Experience
Scouts attend camp with their unit and enjoy the traditional Scouts BSA summer camp experience. Campsites will be assigned based on unit registration, attendance, and availability.
Units should register all youth and adult leaders who will be attending camp.
Registration Information
Please provide accurate information for each participant during registration, including emergency contact information, dietary needs, allergies, and any accommodations or special considerations that camp staff should be aware of.
Additional information regarding check-in, medical forms, campsite assignments, merit badge and program registration, what to bring, meals, and the camp schedule will be provided before your arrival at camp.
Adult Leader Registration
Units will receive one (1) free adult leader registration for every five (5) Scouts registered for summer camp, up to a maximum of two (2) free adult leaders per unit.
5 registered Scouts = 1 adult leader FREE
10 or more registered Scouts = 2 adult leaders FREE
Additional adult leaders may attend at the published adult leader rate.
Free adult registrations are based on the unit's final number of registered Scouts attending camp.
Come Experience Camp Moses!
Summer camp is more than just a week at camp. It is an opportunity for Scouts to challenge themselves, learn new skills, grow in confidence and leadership, and experience the fun and fellowship that make Scouting special.
We look forward to welcoming your unit to Camp Moses for an amazing summer!

/234-WHOA.desc:
Looking for something different to do on your Saturday?
Come spend the day outdoors at Camp Moses with Woronoco Heights Outdoor Adventures (WHOA!)!
WHOA! is a fun, family-friendly outdoor adventure program featuring different activities throughout the year. Whether you are a Scout, coming with your family, or simply looking for something new to try, everyone is welcome!
Bring a friend, explore Camp Moses, learn a new skill, and enjoy a great day outdoors!
What Are the Adventures?
Every WHOA! weekend is a little different!
Programs are offered on select Saturdays during September, October, November, January, February, March, April, May, and often June.
Depending on the season and the month, activities may include:
Ice Fishing
Snowshoeing
Rifle & Shotgun Shooting
Outdoor Cooking
ATVs
*
Blacksmithing
Ham Radio
Outdoor Skills
And much more!
Activities change from month to month, giving you a reason to come back and try something new!
Please note: Details for each month's activities will generally be available one to two weeks before the event. For more information about the activities, please see the attached flyer.
*
Important ATV Requirements: Participants must be 14 years of age or older and must have earned their ATV license in order to participate in the ATV activity.
Bring Your Family & Make New Friends!
WHOA! is open to everyone ages 5 and older — you do not have to be a Scout to participate!
Come with your Scout unit, bring your family, or invite a friend.
Some activities may have additional age or participation requirements for safety. The activities available to each participant will depend on their age and the program being offered that month.
When Does the Fun Start?
WHOA! runs from:
9:00 AM – 3:00 PM
You don't have to stay for the entire day. Participants are welcome to arrive and leave at any time during the program.
Check-in: Trading Post at Camp Moses
How Much Does All This Fun Cost?
A full day of outdoor adventure is:
Youth  $10.00 per person
Adults $10.00 per person
Your registration gives you access to the scheduled WHOA! activities available for your age group that day.
What Should I Wear?
Remember—these are outdoor adventures!
Please dress appropriately for the season and expected weather conditions.
Good footwear is especially important. Many WHOA! activities involve walking around Camp Moses, where the ground may be uneven, wet, snowy, or muddy.
Boots or other sturdy, closed-toe shoes are the best choice, especially during spring mud season.
Important Footwear Safety Rule
Open-toed shoes, Crocs, and sandals are not permitted at camp.
For everyone's safety, please wear sturdy, closed-toe footwear while participating in WHOA! activities.
Rain or Shine — The Adventure Continues!
Our weekend programs run rain or shine, so please check the weather and come prepared!
Depending on the season, that might mean bringing rain gear, warm layers, gloves, boots, sunscreen, or other appropriate outdoor clothing.
A little weather doesn't stop a WHOA! adventure!
Sign Me Up!
Pre-registration is strongly encouraged.
Registering ahead of time helps our staff prepare activities, equipment, and supplies and lets us know how many participants to expect.
Made a last-minute decision to join us? Come on out!  participants are welcome to attend.
Bring your family. Bring a friend. Try something new.
Come see what makes you say… WHOA!
We look forward to seeing you at Camp Moses for Woronoco Heights Outdoor Adventures!

/250-113657.desc:
Northern Star Council
College of Commissioner Service
November 13, 2027
The College of Commissioner Service (CCS) is designed to help our volunteer serving commssioners grow in their role and continue their knowledge of practices that benefit their units. The college is being held November 13, 2027 in-person at Northern Star Council's Leadership Center and Base Camp, and with virtual program options.
Basic Commissioner - Bachelor’s Degree – Master’s Degree – Doctorate Degree - Advanced Studies - Continuing Education
What Course Do I Register For:
Basic Commissioner Training:
Basic Commissioner training will be offered for new commissioners.
Bachelors of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Bachelors Program is the level of training available to anyone who has completed Commissioner Basic Training. This training will offer a series of 8 courses like practical solutions to common unit problems and serving Scouts with special needs. These and other courses will add to your Basic Training skills.
Masters of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Master’s program is advanced training that follows Bachelor of Commissioner Service training. This training provides 8 hours of advanced training to teach critical skills that allow commissioners to assist units leaders with concepts such as "Facilitation skills and other" and skills to help develop new leaders. You'll broaden your commissioner skills to effectively work with specific unit needs or special needs of Scouts.
Doctorate of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Doctorate program is next level of training after the Master’s Degree and includes carrying out a project that will benefit Scouting.  Students will attend 8 hours of advanced level training courses that includes the presentation of your final project. Interested candidtes must contact the Dean of Doctorate College for registration approval. See the course booklet for contact information.
Advanced Studies Degree:
The Advanced Studies Program provides 8 hours of elective course curriculum that supplements other commissioner training. The Advanced studies Program is intended for commissioners who have already completed the Master’s or Doctorate programs and are interested in gaining further knowledge from a wide range of topics.
Continuing Education:
A non-degree opportunity for commissioners of any level to participate in a group discussion on key unit issues commissioners need to address. A great way to stay current with changes and new requirements in Scouting.
College of Commissioner Service website:
More information on the College of Commissioner Service can be found at: http://www.northernstarbsa.org/about-the-college-of-commissioner-service
Please note that any prior degree from any College of Commissioner Service will qualify you to attend the next training level.

/250-NorthWind2027.desc:
Winter Camp Program Catalog
Enjoy an outfitted weekend of winter fun with our trained Winter Camp Staff in January or February. Staying warm is easy when we provide cold weather training, winter clothing, camping equipment, excellent meals, and outdoor activities. Our tiered programs and commitment to innovation ensures fun for all experience levels a new challenges each winter.
Please review the Winter Camp Program Catalog with all your families. This catalog includes information on programs, dates, costs, what to bring, how to plan and much more. A link to the Catalog can be found above.
Snow Base
For more dates and availability, see the
Snow Base registration page
. Snow Base offers many of the same programs as North Wind, but is based out of Tomahawk Scout Reservation in Birchwood, WI. For more information, see the Winter Camping Catalog (linked above).
Fees and Deposits
A deposit is required per person to hold a spot in a program. Deposits range from $25 per person to $100 per person, depending on the program. To register you must provide names, ages, gender, and winter camping experience.
The balance of your crew fees is due to the Northern Star Council office on December 15th. Because of the limited number of places available, each weekend due to equipment and lodging limitations, crews are responsible for the number of participants that they registered.
Adult Leadership Requirements
Each troop needs to provide two-deep leadership while on the property. If your troop has Scouts in three different programs on the same weekend you must have a minimum of one registered adult leader in each program and maintain one adult for every four youth.
Other Information
Before Departure
Review the
Packing List
with your Scouts. Please remember your face coverings. Make sure that Scouts are not packing cotton clothing to wear on trail. You do not need to request gear in advance. This will be checked out in our outfitting area at camp.
Collect
Health Forms (Parts A&B)
for all Scouts and Leaders. Be ready to turn these in at check-in. We will keep Part A, you can get Part B back if requested.
If you’d like to get a jump start on winter camping principles, here’s a video created last year
Winter Camping Principles Video
. This will review safety rules, first aid, cold weather basics, and review the gear you need to bring and what we provide.
Arrival
Plan to arrive between 7:30pm and 8:00pm on Friday night. (Doesn’t apply to ice fishing or the Experience program)
Please note that the Experience, Search and Rescue, and Ice Fishing programs start on Saturday morning
- please do not show up on Friday night without prior approval as we will not have planned space for you.
Map to North Wind(Stearns)
--
Map of North Wind(Stearns)
When you arrive, you will be greeted by our staff in the parking lot. They will direct you to your bunkroom.
Friday Night Items (Doesn’t apply to Experience, Search and Rescue, and Ice Fishing programs)
Arriving on time is important. There is a lot to cover on Friday night. Arriving late will may delay departure on trail and make it hard to complete all your winter activities. Here are the tasks planned for Friday night:
Get settled into your bunkroom.
Check out winter camping gear (Participants of the Experience Program will do this on Saturday morning).
Review Winter Camping Principles with your guide
Review Activity Plan and complete Trip Plan
Pack Gear Sleds
Pack Trail Food
Schedules
Schedules can be found in the Program Catalog linked above.
Food Service
We provide Gluten Free, Vegetarian, Peanut Free, Lactose Free, and Pork-Free options. If you have someone that needs to bring their own food, please contact us directly with their needs and we’ll walk through the menu with you to determine what they need to supplement.
Departure
Scouts usually leave camp around 1:30pm on Sunday. Units can leave earlier if needed. If leaving early, you may miss activities on Sunday morning.
Cancelation Policy
All Camp Northern Star

/250-TSCSailing27.desc:
Embark on an unforgettable journey this summer with our weekly sailing and camping adventure in the majestic Apostle Islands!
Each week, join a small group of 8 total explorers for a 4-day, 3-night expedition aboard a sailboat. Navigate the clear waters of Lake Superior, marvel at breathtaking sea caves and towering sandstone cliffs, and discover hidden coves perfect for swimming and sunbathing.
Your adventure includes:
Expert instruction:
No sailing experience needed! Our experienced captain will guide you through the basics of sailing, ensuring a safe and enjoyable experience.
Comfortable accommodations:
Relax while sailing as the sailboat is equipped with comfortable sleeping quarters and a fully equipped kitchen.
Learn new skills:
See how larger sailboats run and operate, learn from an experienced boat captain, and learn how navigation systems can autopilot a boat.
Unforgettable memories:
Create lasting memories and forge new friendships with your fellow adventurers.
Details:
Capacity:
Each week, we can have 8 people join in on the program. The boat captian does not count towards this 8-person limit, so an ideal crew would be 2 adults and 6 youth from the same unit. You can also request spots for a half crew of 3 scouts and 1 adult and be paired with another half crew.
Age Requirement:
Participants must be 13 years of age or going into 8th grade to participate.
Program Request:
This program has a very limited capacity, and as such we will start the sign up process with a Program Request Period. If we have more sign-ups for a week than spots in a week, we will randomly select groups to fill the space.
You do not need to enter names during the program request period, but you will need to designate the gender of the participants
Price:
The price for the entire week is $700 for both youth and adults. There is a $200 deposit per half crew (4 people) and a $400 deposit per full crew (8 people).
The deposit is fully refundable or transferrable to summer camp at Tomahawk Scout Camp for those who are not placed into the program.
Transportation:
You will need to provide your own transportation to Bayfield, WI.
Food: Food is not included
and will need to be purchased on your way up. We will share an example menu with food that will pack and cook well while sailing. We recommend stopping in Hayward to pick up food, as there are very few cities on the way up.
Dates:
This program is offered every week Tomahawk Scout Camp is running.
You will select your preferred week when registering, but we also ask if you are available for any other weeks
so you only need to register once.
Registrations:
Registrations will be transferred to Tomahawk after registration opens for individuals in March.
Schedule:
On the first day of your session, Sunday, you will check in as usual to Tomahawk Scout Camp.
On Monday, we will go over sailing basics, basic chart reading, food plans (see above), and other necessary information for the trip.
On Tuesday, you will depart for the Apostle Islands and will pick up food along the way. Then, you will meet the boat captain, get the grand tour, then depart!
From Tuesday night through Friday, you'll spend most of your time on the boat sailing. You will sail around the Apostle Islands, take in the views, swim and visit a one or two of the sites.
At night the boat will be anchored or docked at one of the Apostle Islands.  All participants will sleep on the boat.
You'll spend Friday night at your campsite at Tomahawk, then head back home the following morning
Book your summer adventure today and set sail for an unforgettable experience in the Apostle Islands!

Sioux Camp
If operating under the Patrol Method is what your Troop/Crew is looking for, then Sioux is the place for you! Sioux's campsites are designed with the Patrol Method in mind. Breakfast, lunch, and supper ingredients delivered to campsite and cooked by patrol. Sioux has 15 different campsites most of which are directly on the lake!
See our
Summer Camp Planning page
for more information about planning for camp.
*Linked Troops: Our reservation system is currently set up to only allow same-gender units to book a shared site, but we do allow linked boy and girl troops to share sites. The leader booking the site will need to contact us at
tomahawk@northernstar.org
so we can place the linked troops in the same site.
*Are your scouting families interested in joining you at Tomahawk? Why not book a cabin or tent/RV site at Family Island? For more info, please visit the Family Island page:
Family Island

/250-TSCWhitePine2027.desc:
TOMAHAWK SCOUT CAMP
White Pine Camp
Food Service: Outdoor Dining Hall, 3 Meals/Day
White Pine is our newest subcamp and is a great experience for those looking for a smaller camp feel. The areas around White Pine's shoreline have beautiful views, and with hilly terrain the tenting sites are all on raised wooden platforms, giving an experience unique from the other subcamps. White Pine's tenting areas aren't the only unique feature! All meals are served in giant outdoor dining pavilions, located on the North or South end of camp. The staff at White Pine are always willing to put on a show at lunch and dinner! White Pine has 10 campsites, all of which are on the lake!
See our
Summer Camp Planning page
for more information about planning for camp.

/250-aol2027.desc:
Arrow of Light Camp is open to Arrow of Light Scouts (entering 5th grade in the fall). This camp is designed to help Scouts complete advancement and introduce them to Scouts BSA. They can look forward to an extra night at camp, as well as some unique activities that are not available to them at Cub Summer Camp.
Camp will include activities such as climbing, obstacle courses, outdoor skills, advancement opportunities, and more!
Food service will be provided in a dining hall (Miles Hall). A ratio of 1 adult for every 4 youth is required. Please make one reservation per Pack.
For info and an FAQ about Early Registration (June 1st - January 31st)

/250-ccs2026.desc:
Northern Star Council
College of Commissioner Service
November 14, 2026
The College of Commissioner Service (CCS) is designed to help our volunteer serving commssioners grow in their role and continue their knowledge of practices that benefit their units. The college is being held November 14, 2026 in-person at Northern Star Council's Leadership Center and Base Camp, and with virtual program options.
See the full Course Catalog at the link for More information-Course Catalog located below the register button on the right side of this page.
Basic Commissioner - Bachelor’s Degree – Master’s Degree – Doctorate Degree - Advanced Studies - Continuing Education
What Course Do I Register For:
Basic Commissioner Training:
Basic Commissioner training will be offered for new commissioners.
Bachelors of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Bachelors Program is the level of training available to anyone who has completed Commissioner Basic Training. This training will offer a series of 8 courses like practical solutions to common unit problems and serving Scouts with special needs. These and other courses will add to your Basic Training skills.
Masters of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Master’s program is advanced training that follows Bachelor of Commissioner Service training. This training provides 8 hours of advanced training to teach critical skills that allow commissioners to assist units leaders with concepts such as "Facilitation skills and other" and skills to help develop new leaders. You'll broaden your commissioner skills to effectively work with specific unit needs or special needs of Scouts.
Doctorate of Commissioner Service Degree:
The Doctorate program is next level of training after the Master’s Degree and includes carrying out a project that will benefit Scouting.  Students will attend 8 hours of advanced level training courses that includes the presentation of your final project. Interested candidtes must contact the Dean of Doctorate College for registration approval. See the course booklet for contact information.
Advanced Studies Degree:
The Advanced Studies Program provides 8 hours of elective course curriculum that supplements other commissioner training. The Advanced studies Program is intended for commissioners who have already completed the Master’s or Doctorate programs and are interested in gaining further knowledge from a wide range of topics.
Continuing Education:
A non-degree opportunity for commissioners of any level to participate in a group discussion on key issues commissioners need to address. A great way to stay current with changes and new requirements in Scouting.
College of Commissioner Service website:
More information on the College of Commissioner Service can be found at: http://www.northernstarbsa.org/about-the-college-of-commissioner-service
Please note that any prior degree from any College of Commissioner Service will qualify you to attend the next training level.

As part of our commitment to reach the widest possible audience, Northern Star Scouting offers a series of Instructor-led Zoom/TEAMS classes for Adult Leaders online. There is no cost for these sessions.
We will be updating the class listings regularly as we confirm new sessions.
Additionally, you may request a topic by emailing UoS Extension Co-ordinator, Rachel Thiemann, at ExtensionUoS@gmail.com
.

/251-116946.desc:
This is a two weekend course.  You must attend both weekends in full!
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home units and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must KNOW, and what a leader must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
NYLT content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ the leadership skills much faster.
NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and audio-visual support, NYLT participants will be engaged in a unified approach to leadership that will give them the skill and confidence to lead well. Through a wide range of activities, games, and adventures, participants will work and play together as they put into action the best Scouting has to offer.
During the course, participants must wear Class B shirts. Two shirts are included with registrations; additional shirts may be ordered for a fee.
In order to attend a NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a completed CampDoc Health record.
Scouts BSA members (male and female) must be at least
13 and ranked a First Class Scout or highe
r. They must have completed
Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops
.
Venturers and Sea Scouts (male and female) must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation. The form is found under attachments.

/251-116965.desc:
IOLS stands for Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills, a hands-on training course for adult leaders in Scouting America.
It provides the basic outdoor skills needed to lead Scouts, including camping, cooking, rope work, first aid, and navigation.
Completion of IOLS, along with other requirements, is mandatory for Scoutmasters and assistant Scoutmasters to be considered "trained".
What you will learn..
Core Outdoor Skills:  The training focuses on teaching the practical outdoor skills found in the Scouts BSA Handbook, covering the basics needed to achieve early ranks.
Patrol Method: Participants work in patrols to learn how to lead and manage a Scout-led troop.
Camp Skills: You will gain confidence in setting up camp, cooking, and using tools.
Navigation: Skills like map reading, compass use, and hiking techniques are taught.
Outdoor Ethics and Safety: The course emphasizes safe practices and respect for the outdoors.
Who should attend All adult leaders in Scouts BSA troops and Varsity Scout Teams. Venturing crew advisors who are engaged in outdoor programs. Assistant Scoutmasters and Scoutmasters who need to complete their training.
Why it's important It provides a working knowledge of the basic outdoor skills necessary to succeed as a leader. It builds confidence and competence in leading youth on outdoor adventures. It ensures leaders can effectively teach Scouts the skills needed for rank advancement.
It's a requirement for leaders to be considered "trained" for many positions.

/251-117440.desc:
Get ready to feast on competition at the inaugural Mayflower Scoutsgiving!
This high-stakes, day-long event invites your Patrol to step back into the spirit of the pilgrims and the Wampanoag, testing your survival skills and teamwork in a quest for the ultimate prize.
Think of it as a Klondike Derby without the snow, where the grit of the wilderness meets the gratitude of the season. Patrols will navigate a series of skill-based "ports," competing in classic Scouting challenges like precision fire-building, pioneer lashing, and emergency first aid.
Every knot tied and signal sent brings your team one step closer to the ultimate glory: winning the first-ever Mayflower "Gravy Boat" Trophy.
This isn't just a win—it’s a seat at the head of the table for a year of bragging rights.
After the dust settles and the winners are crowned, we’ll transition from the field to the Dining Hall for a massive, traditional Thanksgiving Dinner.
We’ll celebrate our hard work and shared Scouting bond with a full spread of turkey, sides, and all the trimmings. It’s a day of grit, a night of gratitude, and an experience your Patrol won’t want to miss.

/251-AdvOvernight2026.desc:
Unleash Your Inner Adventurer at Adventure Overnight Camp!
Four Days of Thrilling Activities, Lasting Friendships, and Unforgettable Memories for Webelos Scouts.
Are you ready for the summer of a lifetime? Our Adventure Overnight Camp is the ultimate destination for Webelos Scouts seeking excitement, growth, and pure, unadulterated fun! Designed for youth entering grades 4 & 5 in the fall of 2027,
This immersive experience will transform your summer into an epic adventure.
What to Expect:
Action-Packed Days
: Dive into a world of thrilling activities, including archery, BB shooting, swimming, hiking, fishing, boating, and a variety of sports and games. There's never a dull moment!
Creative Exploration
: Unleash your artistic side with crafts, leatherwork, and woodworking. Learn new skills and create lasting keepsakes.
Outdoor Skills & Adventure
: Experience the thrill of fishing in our pristine pond, navigating the waters by boat, and exploring lush forest trails.
Campfire Magic
: As the sun sets, gather around the campfire for captivating stories, engaging challenges, and breathtaking stargazing.
Friendship & Camaraderie
: Share a tent with a buddy, join a den, and forge lifelong friendships with fellow Webelos.
Personal Growth
: Participate in daily flag ceremonies, share campsite duties, and develop valuable life skills while having fun.
"Polar Bear" Plunge
: For the brave souls, take part in our popular early morning "Polar Bear" swim!
Delicious Meals
: Enjoy communal meals, participate as waiters, and learn about teamwork and responsibility.
Age-Appropriate Activities
: Our program is specifically designed for Webelos, ensuring a safe, engaging, and enjoyable experience.
Why Choose Adventure Overnight Camp?
Prepare for Future Scouting Adventures
: This program introduces Webelos to adventure programs and camp activities, preparing them for more rigorous Scouting endeavors.
Build Confidence and Independence
: Webelos will gain confidence by trying new things and taking on new challenges in a supportive environment.
Create Lasting Memories
: The memories made at Adventure Overnight Camp will last a lifetime.
No Experience Required
: All you need is a desire to have fun!
Who Can Attend?
Webelos and Arrow of Light Scouts entering grades 4 & 5 in the fall of 2027.
Packs and dens are welcome to attend together, or Webelos can join individually.
Every Scout is encouraged to bring a friend!
Don't Miss Out!
This is your chance to experience the ultimate summer adventure. Our program fills up quickly, so don't delay!
Ready to embark on an unforgettable adventure? Register for Adventure Overnight Camp today!

: August 8-11, 2027, a half week
Arrival

: 4pm on August 11

/251-Baloo11072026.desc:
Welcome to BALOO training in the Mayflower Council!
The Cub Scout leader training is required for any Cub Scout den or pack outdoor event, including pack camping overnighters, Webelos den, and Arrow of Light den overnighters.
The Mayflower council training team will be presenting this training as an overnight, day-and-a-half training.
BALOO training comprises two components—an online component and a practical, hands-on component. Both must be completed to qualify as a “TRAINED” Cub Scout outdoor leader.
The online component must be completed before the practical component. The online training contains introductory and basic information to be built upon during the practical training.
Why Take BALOO?

/251-CampSquanto2027.desc:
Ignite Your Troop's Spirit at Camp Squanto: The Ultimate Adventure Awaits!
Hey Unit Leaders! Are you ready to give your Scouts a summer they'll NEVER forget? Camp Squanto is the place where ordinary weeks turn into legendary adventures. We're not just offering a summer camp; we're offering a life-changing experience that builds character, forges friendships, and unleashes the true spirit of Scouting!
Why Camp Squanto is the #1 Choice for Your Troop:
Unleash Adventure:
Camp Squanto is a launchpad for adventure! We're talking action-packed days filled with aquatics, Scoutcraft, target and range sports, and a massive menu of merit badge opportunities. Your Scouts will conquer challenges, discover new skills, and create stories they'll tell for years to come.
Forge Stronger Bonds:
Camp Squanto isn't just about individual growth; it's about troop unity. Scouts will learn to work together, support each other, and build the kind of camaraderie that only comes from shared adventures.
Effortless Planning, Maximum Impact:
We know you're busy, and we're here to help! Our detailed Leader's Guide and dedicated staff make pre-camp planning a breeze. From easy check-in to well-organized programs, we handle the details so you can focus on what matters most: your Scouts.
Safety and Support:
We prioritize safety above all else. Our experienced staff are trained in Youth Protection and dedicated to creating a nurturing environment where every Scout can thrive. We're here to support your Scouts (and you!) every step of the way.
Ready to Lead Your Troop on an Unforgettable Journey?
Contact us
today to secure your spot at Camp Squanto and give your Scouts the summer of a lifetime!

/251-CitizenshipintheWorldMB111506.desc:
Citizenship in the World Merit Badge at the Nature Center
Date:
Sunday, November 15, 2026
Time:
12:00 – 1:30 PM
Where:
South Shore YMCA Nature Center, 48 Jacobs Lane, Norwell, MA 02061
Capacity:
26 Scouts
What to Bring:
Requirements handwritten in a notebook or typed, printed, and brought to the Merit
Badge Course for complete credit!
Requirements to complete BEFORE session:
#1, 3B, 7A & 7B
Join our Merit Badge Counselors at the South Shore YMCA Nature Center for an opportunity to work
toward your Citizenship in the World Merit Badge!
This program will help Scouts explore what it means to be a citizen of a global community. We’ll discuss
different cultures, international relationships, global organizations, and the ways people and countries
work together to address challenges that affect us all.
Scouts will learn about their responsibilities as citizens of the world and explore how communication,
cooperation, and understanding different perspectives can help create a more connected and respectful
world.
Come ready to learn, participate, and expand your perspective as we explore what it means to be a
citizen of the world!
Registration is required in advance. Limited spaces available – sign up early to secure your spot!
Check-in will begin at 12:00 PM with the Badge session starting at 12:10 PM.

Calling all adventurous Scouts!
Are you ready to turn navigation into a high-tech, outdoor treasure hunt? Join us at the Hull Lifesaving Museum Boathouse on Saturday, October 10th for an exciting, hands-on day of exploration, learning, and fun as we conquer the Geocaching Merit Badge!

The Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS) course is a hands-on, 24-hour outdoor training program.
It gives adult leaders in Scouting America the practical skills needed to guide youth safely and with confidence in the outdoors.
Required for Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters to be considered position-trained.
Patrol Method:
Modeled as a youth-led troop where adults work together in patrols.
Class Focus:
Prepares leaders to teach basic outdoor skills required for ranks up to First Class.

Campsite Setup:
Choosing proper tent sites and pitching tents.
Cooking & Sanitation:
Outdoor meal planning, cooking techniques, and safe camp hygiene.
Woods Tools:
Safe use and care of pocket knives, axes, and saws.
Ropes:
Practical knots, bends, hitches, and lashings.
Navigation:
Reading maps and using a compass.
Outdoor Ethics:
Principles of Leave No Trace and nature identification.
Campfire Programs
: Planning and running a campfire program.
Working as patrols, this hands-on course provides adult leaders the practical outdoor skills they need to lead.
The Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills training course is a day and a half long.

/251-RadioMB2026.desc:
Are you ready to discover the invisible world of radio signals, global broadcasts, and wireless technology?
Join New England Sci Tech
this fall for a hands-on, multi-session deep dive into the fascinating science of radio! Whether you’re curious about how cell phones instantly stream video, how radio waves bounce around the world, or how amateur "ham" radio operators stay connected during emergencies when all other systems go down, this series has something for you.
Under the guidance of experienced instructors at New England Sci Tech, Scouts will explore everything from electromagnetic spectrum diagrams to live station operations!
Class Details & Schedule
Dates: November 7, 14, 21 & December 5, 12, 19
Time: 9:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Location: New England Sci Tech Attendance
Requirement: Scouts must attend all 6 sessions to satisfy all badge requirements and earn the Radio Merit Badge.
What You’ll Learn & Do:
Radio Safety & Fundamentals:
Master circuit grounding, electrical burn first aid, and battery safety, while mapping out the electromagnetic spectrum from AM/FM radio to Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
The Science of Radio Waves:
Discover how radio signals travel across the globe, learn the difference between local and DX (distance) stations, and explore modulation techniques like AM, FM, and Morse Code.
Hands-On Operation:
Use proper call signs and the NATO phonetic alphabet to carry out and log a real or simulated radio contact!
Prerequisites & Preparation
Please review the requirements and be prepared to participate in interactive discussions and hands-on demonstrations each week!
Space is limited to 8 Scouts to ensure a quality hands-on experience—reserve your spot today!

/251-WRFA032027.desc:
The primary purpose of the American Red Cross Wilderness and Remote First Aid course is to provide individuals a foundation of first aid principles and skills to be able to respond to emergencies and give care in areas that do not have immediate emergency medical services (EMS) response, such as wilderness and remote environments, including urban disasters, such as earthquakes and hurricanes. This class is based on the American Red Cross Wilderness and Remote First Aid syllabus.
This class is open to adults and youth (14 years and older).
A current CPR certification is required to complete the class, but not required before taking Wilderness and Remote First Aid.  Only the following BSA Approved CPR Programs are accepted:
•    American Heart Association
•    American Red Cross
•    Emergency Care & Safety Institute (ECSI)
•    American Safety & Health Institute (also known as Health & Safety Institute)
The certification must include Adult CPR and must also include a hands-on skills session as well.  No “online only” classes will be accepted.
Hours are 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Saturday and Sunday, paricipants MUST attend both days.

/272-2027NYLT.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training
Training youth leaders in Scouting is important for promoting individual youth growth and for providing a leadership model for the Scout BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouting (unit) programs. The unit leader is the primary source of youth leader training. As a supplement to that training, the National Youth Leader Training course provides youth with a one-week or two-weekend-long experience – a month in the life of a model unit - designed to give potential youth leaders the skills they can use to lead their units. The objectives of the course are:
Develop a youth’s confidence and knowledge in leading the unit’s program.
Gain a working understanding of the resources, skills, and methods needed to undertake further unit leadership responsibility.
Share ideas and learn from the experiences of other youths from units across the council.
Support adult unit leaders in training youth leaders in the unit.
Reinforce a youth’s relationship with his unit leader and other adult leaders.
Experience Scouting/Venturing at its very best.
Who is Eligible to Attend NYLT?
NYLT is designed for those Scouts/Venturers/Sea Scouts who are likely to serve in senior leadership roles in their unit in the near future.  Scouts selected should be made aware that this is NOT a summer camp program and that it involves classroom-style and hands-on training sessions.
To attend an NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA must be 13 years of age and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program registration. They must be a First Class Scout and have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience.

/272-CCBSBSA27.desc:
Thank you for choosing Cole Canoe Base as the destination for your 2027 Summer Camping experience!
Edward N. Cole Canoe Base is a 1,489 acre piece of wilderness, nestled along the banks of the beautiful Rifle River in Ogemaw County, Michigan. We are one of the premier summer camping destinations for thousands of youth and adult leaders from all over the Midwest for over 50 years. We are owned and operated by the Michigan Crossroads Council of the Boy Scouts of America.
Are you and your unit looking for a traditional summer camping program? We offer scouts opportunities to earn over 95 merit badges during our week long summer camp program. We also offer nightly camp wide events, and daily programs designed to let scouts choose their own activities, providing opportunities for scouts to advance their skills in athletics, crafts, and basic scout skills, cooking, swimming and boating. This past summer camping season we have a unit return rate of over 85%.
We're proud to be a patrol cooking camp. This means daily meals are prepared in your campsite by youth and adults. No waiting in line at the dining hall here! Just pick up your ingredients from the commissary and take them back to camp to prepare our simple but filling, dietician approved menu. Don't like what's on the menu? Swap it out for one of our alternative meal options!
Our high adventure program provides older scouts an opportunity to stray from the traditional summer camp experience and put their outdoor skills to the test, on canoe trips on three of Michigan's most scenic rivers- the Rifle River, the Fox-Manistique, and the Au Sable. We also are hosts to the ATV Safety Institue's ATV Rider course and offer trail rides in and out of base camp.
There's too much to do in one week so don't forget to consider a 2nd week on your own or book a high adventure trip just for the older scouts! We can accommodate units of any size!

/272-CRSBSA27.desc:
Thank you for choosing Camp Rotary as the destination for your 2027 Summer Camping experience!
* For the quickest possible response, please contact us via email *
History tells us that Lake Beebe was, from early times, used by the Ottawa, Potawatomi and Chippewa Indians as camping and fishing grounds. During some periods they used the area as a more permanent site. These tribes did not use tepees but lived in dome-shaped lodges covered with wood bark. Lake Beebe, a beautiful spring-fed lake approximately 30 acres in size with towering pines in the surrounding acreage lies not far northeast of Clare, Michigan and is centered in a 1,164 acre tract.
In 1924 the camp at Lake Arnold became inadequate for the growing area Boy Scout Council. Members of The Saginaw Rotary Club became aware of this problem and, with Boy Scout executives began to look for a new site. Beebe Lake, located on a 440 acre site just north of Clare, was inspected. The search team was particularly impressed with the beauty, location, and adaptability of the place. The Boy Scouts moved into the camp at the end of August of 1925 and immediately began projects for improvement to make the grounds suitable for a Boy Scout Camp. A mess hall was built, a bathing beach was prepared, and a new dam was built which raised the lake level by four feet. In 1932 an additional 40 acres was purchased, in 1950 another 40 acres, and in 1964 another 583 acres making the total 1,063.
Summer Camp at Camp Rotary features: 64 different Merit Badges, Exciting evening programs, Family Style meals in the Dining Hall, Inflatables and Stand Up Paddleboards!
We hope to see you out on Lake Beebe and on our many acres of beautiful camp this coming summer!

This weekend will be very similar to our ever popular Polar Bear campout, with one main exception.  All participants will sleep inside all weekend!

If you’re looking for a winter rafting wilderness adventure that will build character, skills, and lifelong memories, then this is the trip for you and your Troop. The Pine River Winter Jam rafting trip will challenge Scouts and Venturers to turn off all the distractions around them and become immersed in the now—to explore outside. And most importantly, it’s the opportunity to instill a lifelong love of the being outdoors during all seasons in our Scouts.
But we know that heading into the backcountry with a Troop can be challenging, so we’ve taken care of all the logistics necessary to get your Scouts ready for this trek of a lifetime. We will be providing guided rafting down the beautiful Pine River in northern Michigan, utilizing the Pine River Paddle Sports equipment and staff. Following the float, your Scouts will experience a wilderness snowshoe hike through some of the most picturesque views of the river.
Your Troop will need know the following:
Winter clothing appropriate for the weather
Scouts should be at least 13 years old to participate
Leaders must have proof of completing Safety Afloat training (ratio of 1 trained adult:10 scouts)
Units are responsible for bringing their lunch and snacks for the day
Camping is available through the Silver Creek State Forest Campground. Here is a link to more information:
https://www2.dnr.state.mi.us/parksandtrails/Details.aspx?id=600&type=SFCG
This is a day activity. If units choose to camp, they will need to follow Scouting rules and regulations and the Guide to Safe Scouting.
High-quality inflatable rafts, river equipment including paddle, and personal flotation device (PFD) will be provided by Pine River Paddle Sports.
All participants should know, understand, and respect the rules and procedures for safe boating activities provided by Safety Afloat guidelines. Please Review Safety Afloat with your Scouts prior to arriving for our adventure:
https://www.scouting.org/health-and-safety/gss/gss02/#j
(This is a good learning opportunity for your Scouts to practice preparing a float plan for their excursion)
Transfers from the pull out at the end of the float trip back to the campground will be available upon request, but it will be encouraged for Scouts and Leaders to utilize the second part of the adventure snowshoeing back to the launch.
Snowshoes will be provided, but if a Scout or Leader is interested in bringing their own they can. We can have these staged at the end of the float trip for you or your Scout.
Scouting Annual Health and Medical Record A&B will be required for all participants
Two launch times are being offered – 10 am and 1 pm. You are required to pre-register for your preferred launch time.
Please arrive to check-in no later than 9:30 am for the 10:00 am launch.
Please arrive to check-in no later than 12:30 pm for the 1:00 pm launch.
Adventuring isn’t just a trip, it’s an experience you’ll always remember. And the best part? Scouts and Scouters alike will build character, skills, and memories that last a lifetime.
For more information, please contact Adam Segerlind at
scenictrailsadam@gmail.com
or 231-866-0428.

/296-UniversityofScouting2026.desc:
University of Scouting 2026
Fellow Scouts and Scouters,
On behalf of the Central Minnesota Council, we would like to welcome you to the 2026 University of Scouting! This event represents a unique opportunity for our community to come together, strengthen our skills, and enrich the Scouting experience for everyone involved. Our dedicated faculty, staff, and administration have curated an outstanding program for our second year, featuring a wide range of courses that will enhance your journey in Scouting, whether you’re an adult leader or a young Scout.
The core mission of the University of Scouting is to provide a high-quality program for both adult and youth leaders while offering advancement opportunities for our Scouts. Many of the courses and resources available here are not accessible online or through District-level training, making this a one-of-a-kind annual event. We aim to help both adult leaders and Scouts enhance their programs, build leadership skills, and support the overall vision of Scouting America.
Take some time to explore the various colleges and schools offering courses this year. Whether you’re looking to awaken the Cub Scout within you, learn how to guide your Scout to Eagle, how to integrate high adventure into your unit, or even pursue a Scouting degree, there’s something for everyone!
We are also excited to offer merit badge opportunities for our Scouts. We firmly believe that the University of Scouting should be an event for the whole Troop, so we encourage Scouts to take advantage of these opportunities while their leaders participate in training.
We’re looking forward to an exciting and enriching day of learning, growth, and fellowship. We can’t wait to see you in November at the 2026 University of Scouting!

/303-2027NYLT.desc:
NATIONAL YOUTH LEADERSHIP TRAINING
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a two-weekend course.  Scouts must attend both weekends.
In order to attend an NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Must be First Class by the start of the first weekend.
As of March 1, 2023, Scouts BSA members (male and female) must be at least 13. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops.
Venturers and Sea Scouts (male and female) must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.
Exceptions may be granted on age or rank with approval from the course director.
Scholarships are available. Contact the course directior for more information.

Angling Educator
Online course – must attend both evenings
Tuesday, February 2, 6PM-8PM
Thursday, February 4, 6PM-8PM
$10 per person
Will receive certificate and patch
Angling Educator is a four-hour training course for Scouters and Scouts age 15+. It is a national course and is taught by BSA Certified Angling Instructors.  The purpose of the class is to prepare program leaders to teach fishing skills and to plan and run fishing events for their unit, district, or Council. Angling Educators learn age-based and skills-appropriate fishing tools and techniques for simple cane pole and spin cast fishing. With the addition of fishing adventures at every level of Cub Scouts, this is a great time to expand your skills in teaching fishing to youth! The course highlights best practices in both the classroom and in the field. Graduates can:
• Teach Cubs and Scouts to fish and help them be more successful at catching fish.
• Gain knowledge and learn skills that can be enjoyed and shared for a lifetime.
• Improve day camp & summer camp attendance through fishing program options.
• Provide a major tool for recruiting and retaining Cubs and Scouts at the unit and district level.
